## About Access Roles

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-access-roles
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Role Management > About Access Roles
- Last modified: 2026-06-09T01:27Z
- Summary: Information about access roles in the Zscaler Admin Console.

A role determines the set of tasks that [users](https://help.zscaler.com/authentication-service/about-users)can perform based on the permissions. You can provision users and assign roles to them. Each role has specific permissions that allow users to access and manage various [modules](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/dspm-modules-and-global-modules)in the Zscaler Admin Console.

The Access Roles feature provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Configure and manage role-based access control for users in your organization.
- Allow users to access specific modules and perform specific actions depending on the permissions.
- Create custom roles.

## Predefined Roles

DSPM provides the following [predefined roles and permissions](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) that can be assigned to users. You can also [create custom roles](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-roles) and add specific permissions.

- **Administrator**: The default super admin role with the highest level of privilege and has access to all DSPM modules and actions.
- **View-Only Administrator**: A default administrator role with View-Only access to all modules and the permission to export data.
- **Security Officer**: A role with View-Only access to all modules and permissions to perform actions across [Policies](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies), [Investigation](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-investigation), and [Reports](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-reports).
- **IT Administrator**: A role with administrative access to perform actions across [Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts), and [Integrations](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-third-party-integrations).
- **Data Analyst**: A role with administrative and View-Only access to perform actions across [Policies](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies), [Investigation](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-investigation), [Reports](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-reports), [Alerts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alerts), and [Evidence](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-sensitive-data-details).
- **ZIA Viewer**: A role assigned to the Internet & SaaS user to access the dashboard via SSO.
- **DLP Policy Manager**: A role assigned to the Internet & SaaS user to access the dashboard or Policy via SSO.

## **About the Access Roles Page**

On the Access Roles page (Administration > Admin Management > Role Based Access Control > User Access Management), you can do the following:

1. View the list of predefined and custom roles. For each role, you can see:
  - **Role Name**: The name of the role. Click to view the modules assigned to the role. See image.
  - **Role Type**: The type of role (**Predefined**or **Custom**).
  - **Permission Count**: The number of permissions assigned to this role.
2. [Add a custom role.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-and-managing-custom-roles)
3. Search for a specific role in the searchable columns.
4. Export the data as a CSV file.
5. [Modify the table rows and columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
6. [Edit a custom role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-and-managing-custom-roles).
7. [Delete a custom role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-and-managing-custom-roles). You cannot edit or delete predefined roles.
8. Sort the column data.

[Image: View the Role Management page]

[Image: View the modules and global modules assigned to the role]

## About Action Rules

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-action-rules
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Action Rules > About Action Rules
- Last modified: 2026-04-21T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on action rules applied to sensitive data in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Action rules allow you to define the criteria for identifying specific data types and to automatically apply Microsoft Purview Information Protection (formerly Microsoft Information Protection) sensitivity labels to files. For example, you can create an action rule to apply a Confidential label to a file that contains personally identifiable information (PII).

Currently, action rules only support the application of sensitivity labels to Azure file shares and on-premises SMB and NFS file shares based on specific criteria, such as DLP engines (e.g., PII, GDPR) and document types.

Action rules provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Gain visibility into files that are labeled and not labeled.
- Secure sensitive data with consistent, content-based labeling.
- Maintain data integrity and compliance by automatically tagging files containing sensitive data.

## About the Action Rules Page

On the Action Rules page (Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Action Rules), you can do the following:

1. [Add an action rule](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-action-rule). DSPM scans and discovers the sensitivity labels every 12 hours. After you create an action rule, DSPM applies the labels every 4 hours.
2. View the list of action rules. For each action rule, you can see:
  - **Rule Name**: The name of the action rule.
  - **Cloud**: The cloud account type.
  - **Scope**: The scope defined for the action rule. Such as tenant (e.g., Zscaler DSPM Bravo), Azure File Share, and file types (e.g., CSV, DAT) to which the rule applies.
  - **DLP Engines**: The DLP Engines selected to classify sensitive data.
  - **Document Types**: The document types classified by the DLP Engine.
  - **Action**: The action (apply label) performed on the file that meets the rule criteria.
  - **Rule Priority**: The order in which the action rule is applied. The value can range from 1 to 2,000. A lower value (e.g., 1) indicates a higher priority.
  - **Status**: The state (**Enabled**, **Disabled**) of the action rule.
  - **Last Updated**: The date and time the action rule was last updated.
3. Sort the column data.
4. Search for a specific action rule.
5. [Modify the table and its columns.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
6. [Enable or disable the action rule.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-action-rules) By default, the action rule is enabled.
7. [Edit, delete, or update the priority of an action rule.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-action-rules)

[Image: View Action Rules page]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Alert Notifications

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alert-notifications
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Alerts > Alert Notification Rules > About Alert Notifications
- Last modified: 2026-04-15T00:37Z
- Summary: Information on the DSPM alert notification rule in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Alert rules define the criteria for generating alert notifications. The criteria could be the occurrence of specific misconfigurations or [data posture policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies) violations in the [cloud accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts).

You can create alert rules to export alert notifications to [third-party integrations](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-third-party-integrations) (Jira, Slack, etc.) for further investigation and remediation. These alert notifications are sent whenever the alert status changes. For example, you can add an alert rule to export notifications to Jira for high-severity policies. When these policies are triggered and their [alert status](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/alert-status) changes, the notification is sent to Jira.

DSPM must be integrated with third-party tools to export alert notifications. To learn more, see [About Third-Party Integrations](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-third-party-integrations).

The alert rules provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- Send alert notifications to third-party integrations.
- Investigate the alert and take immediate action based on the alert severity.
- Focus on critical alerts.

## About the Alert Notifications Page

On the Alert Notifications page (Administration > Alerts > Alert Notifications), you can do the following:

1. [Add an alert rule.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-alert-notification-rule)
2. Search for a specific alert rule.
3. View the list of alert rules. For each rule, you can see:
  - **Alert Rule Name**: The name of the alert rule. Click to view additional rule details or edit the rule in the alert rule drawer. See image.
  - **Filter Scope**: The scope ([business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units), [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies), tags, etc.) selected for the alert rule.
  - **Integration Type**: The third-party tools to which the alert notifications are sent.
  - **Updated By**: The user who updated the alert rule.
  - **Last Updated**: The date and time the alert rule was last updated.
  - **Created By**: The user who created the alert rule.
  - **Created Date**: The date and time the alert rule was created.
  - **State**: The state (**Enabled**, **Disabled**) of the alert rule. An alert rule is disabled with an exclamation mark indicating that it is invalid in the following scenarios: The third-party tools are not configured while adding the alert rule.; The selected filters in the filter scope are deleted (e.g., policies are deleted, accounts are offboarded, or the business unit is deleted).See image. Click the alert rule to see the reason why the alert rule is disabled. See image. You can enable the alert rule only after at least one filter scope is available and at least one third-party tool is configured.
4. [Modify the table and its columns.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
5. [Enable or disable the alert rule.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-alert-rules) By default, the alert rule is enabled.
6. [Edit or delete an alert rule.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-alert-rules)

[Image: The Alert Notifications page with the alerts rules and page details.]

[Image: The alert rule drawer displaying additional details of the rule.]

[Image: The Alert Notifications page with annotation around an invalid alert rule.]

[Image: Invalid alert rule drawer displaying additional details of the rule.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-alerts","lastmod":"2026-04-15T00:25Z","nid":"1477776"} -->
## About Alerts

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alerts
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Alerts > About Alerts
- Last modified: 2026-04-15T00:25Z
- Summary: Information about DSPM alerts.

DSPM continuously scans your cloud resources against the [policies](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies) enabled in your cloud accounts to identify vulnerabilities and generate alerts. When a policy violation is detected, DSPM generates alerts and sends notifications to recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.

An alert is an outcome of a policy evaluation done on a resource type (e.g., S3 bucket, database). For example, If a security policy is enabled to detect any publicly exposed S3 bucket containing sensitive data, and there are 5 such S3 buckets in your cloud storage, DSPM generates 5 alerts.

Alerts are categorized by severity level to help you prioritize them and take action in a timely manner.

Alerts provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- View and manage alert notifications for any security policy violations detected in the cloud accounts.
- Notify recipients to take action and prevent any potential breaches.
- Stay informed about critical security events.

## About the Alerts Page

On the Alerts page (Administration > Alerts > Alerts), you can see the following tabs:

- Grouped By Policy
- Grouped By Resource
- All Alerts

[Image: The alerts page with annotations around all the alert tabs.]

You can view the policies for which alerts are generated. To learn more, see [Viewing Alerts Grouped by Policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-alerts-grouped-policy).

[Image: The group by policy tab with list of policies for which DSPM alerts are generated.]

You can view the resources for which alerts are generated. To learn more, see [Viewing Alerts Grouped by Resource](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-alerts-grouped-resource).

[Image: The grouped by resource tab displaying the list of resources for which DSPM alerts are generated.]

On the All Alerts tab, you can do the following:

1. [Apply filters to view specific data.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) By default, alerts with an open status are displayed.
2. [Add additional filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
3. Search for specific data in the searchable column. You can also export the search results with the applied filters and download the report as an Excel file.
4. View the list of alerts generated for policy violations. For each alert, you can view:
  - **Alert ID**: The unique identifier for the alert. Clickto [view additional details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-alert-details).
  - **Resource Name**: The name of the resource.
  - **Policy Name**: The policy title.
  - **Policy Category**: The [threat category](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/threat-categories) (**Public Exposure**, **Data Loss**, etc.) to which the policy belongs.
  - **Resource Type**: The type of data store (**AWS EC2 instance**, **AWS S3 bucket**, etc.).
  - **Resource ID**: The unique identifier for the resource.
  - **Risk Level**: The risk level (**Critical**, **High**, **Medium**, or **Low**) of the alert. The risk level of an alert is calculated as the average of the policy severity and the resource impact. For example, if the policy severity is Critical and the resource impact is Medium, then the alert risk level is High.
  - **Alert Status**: The status (**Open**, **Closed**, **Resolved,**and**Snoozed**) of the alert.
  - **Cloud Account**: The unique identifier of the cloud account (**AWS**, **Azure**, **GCP**, **Snowflake**, and **On-Premises**) in which the resource is located.
  - **Created Date**: The date and time the alert was generated.
  - **Last Updated**: The date and time the alert was last updated.
5. Export the data and [download the report](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-reports) as an Excel file.
6. [Modify the table and its columns.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
7. Select any of the following actions:
  - **Resolve**: [Resolve an alert](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-alerts).
  - **Snooze**: [Snooze an alert](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-alerts).
  - **Unsnooze**: Unsnooze the alert. This option is available only when the alert is snoozed.
  - **Reset**: [Reset the alert](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-alerts). This option is available only when the alert is resolved.
8. Select one or multiple alerts to [resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-alerts) them. See image.

[Image: The all alerts tab displaying the list of all alerts generated by DSPM.]

[Image: The actions drop-down menu with list of available actions for the selected alerts.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Business Units

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Role Management > About Business Units
- Last modified: 2026-06-09T01:14Z
- Summary: Information about business units in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Business units are logical containers for cloud accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console. Business units govern DSPM from a role-based access control (RBAC) perspective. Organizations can control and manage user access to data in their cloud accounts. This controlled access helps alleviate security risks and thereby maintain the security posture of your cloud resources.

You must assign users or user groups to the business units. To learn more, see [About Users](https://help.zscaler.com/authentication-service/about-users).

You can onboard your [cloud accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts) and map them to business units. You can also restrict user access to specific business units. For example, you might want to restrict a specific team to view the alerts only for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) Cloud Storage buckets, Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts, or restrict partners to view resources only for a certain set of Microsoft Azure subscriptions.

The Business Unit Management page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Manage cloud accounts within the business unit.
- Control what data can be viewed and what tasks can be performed by users on specific sets of cloud accounts.

## About the Business Unit Management Page

On the Business Unit Management page (Policies > Common Configuration > DSPM > Business Unit Management), you can do the following:

1. View the list of business units. For each business unit, you can see:
  - **Business Unit Name**: The name of the business unit. Click to view the cloud accounts that are assigned to this business unit. Click **Manage**to add or delete a cloud account from the [Cloud Accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts) page. See image.
  - **Account Count**: The number of [cloud accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts) assigned to the business unit.
  - **Created On**: The date and time the business unit was created.
2. Add a business unit. See image.
  1. Click **Add Business Unit**.
  2. In the **Add Business Unit** window, enter a unique name for the business unit.
  3. Click **Create**.
3. Search for specific data in the searchable columns.
4. Sort the column data.
5. [Modify the table and its columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
6. Click the **Actions**icon to edit or delete a business unit. You cannot edit or delete the default business unit.

[Image: The Business Unit Management page displaying the list of default and custom business units.]

[Image: The business unit details page listing the cloud accounts that are assigned.]

[Image: The Add Business Unit window with the name field and Create button.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

## About Cloud Accounts

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > About Cloud Accounts
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:56Z
- Summary: Information about onboarding cloud accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Data security is an important aspect of security practices. Organizations need to ensure that data in their cloud accounts is stored, shared, and transferred securely to the right people and services for the right purpose. It is also crucial to know where the data is located, what type of sensitive data (e.g., credit card numbers, login credentials) exists in your cloud accounts, who has access to it, and how secure the data is to prevent any potential data breach.

DSPM continuously monitors and scans the onboarded cloud accounts for sensitive data and vulnerabilities and generates [alerts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alerts) based on data security [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies) violations. DSPM supports the onboarding of [Amazon Web Services (AWS)](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization) accounts, [Microsoft Azure](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant) subscriptions, and [Google Cloud Platform (GCP)](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-gcp-organization) projects.

Onboarding cloud accounts to DSPM provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Gain visibility into all the data stored in the cloud accounts.
- Detect misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and potential threats that could lead to data breaches.
- Respond to security risks and take necessary action to prevent data breaches.

## About the Cloud Accounts Page

On the Cloud Accounts page (Policies > Common Configuration > DSPM > Cloud Accounts), you can do the following:

1. View the total number of cloud accounts monitored by DSPM across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
2. Manage the cloud accounts:
  1. **Monitoring & Autodetection**: Add new accounts to the monitoring scope and enable autodetection.
  2. **Business Units Mapping**: Assign a different [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/changing-business-unit) to the account.
  3. **Manage Regions**: Select [regions](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-regions) that must be monitored and scanned or configure regions to deploy scanning resources for custom network configuration.
  4. **Manage Custom Tags**: Add, edit, or delete [custom tags](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-custom-tags).
  5. **Manage Notification Emails**: Add email addresses of the recipient to be notified of any configuration or permissions issues while onboarding.
  6. **Managing Orchestrator Network** (Custom): Configure the [orchestrator network](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-orchestrator-network) (applicable only if the **DSPM Connection Status** is failed). To learn more, see [Viewing Orchestrator Status](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-orchestrator-status).
  7. **On Demand Validation**: Validate the [onboarded accounts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/validating-cloud-accounts).
  8. **Configure New Orchestrator**(Zscaler): Change the orchestrator account.
  9. **Delete Account**: [Delete or offboard](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/deleting-onboarded-account) an account. The following features are specific to cloud service providers:
    1. **AWS**: [Manage CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/changing-aws-cloudtrail-details), [Manage Services](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-services), [Manage Evidence](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-configuration), and [Manage Data Events](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-data-events).
    2. **Azure**: [Change Application Details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-application-details-and-client-secret), Manage Private Endpoint, Manage Services, and Manage Evidence.
    3. **GCP**: [Update Service Account](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/updating-gcp-service-account) and [Update Private Key](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/updating-private-key-gcp).
3. Onboard an [AWS organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization), [GCP organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-gcp-organization), or a [Microsoft Azure tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant).
4. View the cloud accounts that are onboarded or being onboarded. Select a cloud account to view the following:
  - While the onboarding process is in progress or if DSPM has encountered issues, you can view the issue or paused step and resume onboarding. See image.
  - When the onboarding process is completed successfully, you can view the following tabs: See image.
    - **Overview**: The onboarding status and the orchestrator details.
    - **Subscriptions**, **Projects**, or **Accounts** (based on the cloud account): [Details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarded-account-details) of the onboarded cloud account.
    - **Issues**: The [issues](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarding-issues) encountered while onboarding.
    - **Roles and Templates**: The [roles](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-roles-and-templates)created while onboarding and templates generated by DSPM.

[Image: The DSPM cloud accounts page with the list of accounts onboarded and the details of the account.]

[Image: Resume the onboarding workflow]

[Image: View the Overview section]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-compliance","lastmod":"2026-04-09T22:09Z","nid":"1514301"} -->
## About Compliance

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-compliance
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Compliance > About Compliance
- Last modified: 2026-04-09T22:09Z
- Summary: Information about the Compliance dashboard displayed in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Compliance refers to the security measures and guidelines that are implemented to comply with the industry-specific security frameworks and regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, etc. DSPM detects policies and DLP engines that fail to comply with the frameworks. This information helps you to resolve the issues and ensure your data is compliant with regulatory standards.

You can view the overall compliance status and the total number of policies that failed to comply with specific frameworks. DSPM provides remediation steps to address the compliance issues.

The Compliance dashboard provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- View the predefined and custom compliance frameworks.
- View the summary of failed policies.
- View the compliance configuration details.
- View the resources that are noncompliant and remediate the issues.
- Add custom compliance frameworks.

## About the Compliance Dashboard

On the Compliance dashboard (Analytics > Data Security > DSPM > Compliance), you can do the following:

1. [Add a custom compliance framework.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-custom-compliance-framework)
2. Show disabled frameworks. When you enable this toggle, the disabled frameworks are displayed at the end and are grayed out.
3. View the compliance frameworks in the following format:
  - Grid
  - Table
4. Click the Actions () icon to do the following:
  - [Enable or disable](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-compliance-frameworks) a predefined or custom framework.
  - [Edit or delete](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-compliance-frameworks) a custom framework. You cannot edit or delete a predefined framework.

[Image: The Compliance dashboard displaying the compliance frameworks and the actions available.]

The compliance frameworks, the number of failed policies against the total number of policies, the type of framework (Predefined or Custom) are displayed as tiles. Click any tile to [view the compliance details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-compliance-details).

[Image: The Compliance dashboard displaying the compliance frameworks in grid view.]

The compliance frameworks are displayed in a table. For each framework, you can see:

- **Framework Name**: The name of the compliance framework. Click to [view the compliance details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-compliance-details).
- **Description**: The description of the framework.
- **Failed Policies**: The number of policies that failed to comply with the framework.
- **Total Policies**: The total number of policies for the framework. If a mapped policy is disabled on the [Policies](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies)page, it is excluded from compliance calculations but is still included in the total policies. If a mapped policy is deleted, it is removed from the framework and is not shown in the [policy list](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-compliance-details). For example, if the total policies for a framework is 100, and 2 policies are deleted from the Policies page, then the total policy count is 98.
- **Enabled**: If the framework is enabled or disabled.
- **Type**: The type (**Predefined**or **Custom**) of framework.

[Image: The Compliance dashboard displaying list of compliance frameworks in a table.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-data-center","lastmod":"2026-05-24T07:06Z","nid":"1526556"} -->
## About On-Premises Data Centers

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-center
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > On-Premises Data Centers and Scanners > On-Premises Data Centers > About On-Premises Data Centers
- Last modified: 2026-05-24T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about on-premises data centers in the Zscaler Admin Console.

An on-premises data center refers to a facility that hosts various IT infrastructure components, including databases, servers, and networking applications, which are managed independently by the organization rather than a cloud service provider. These data centers are typically located within the premises of the organization. On-premises data centers provide organizations with complete control over their data, security, and infrastructure, making them an essential component of many hybrid and on-premises IT environments.

DSPM scans the databases in these on-premises data centers, providing visibility into the sensitive data that is stored in the databases. This allows you to manage and secure the data and maintain a strong security posture.

Onboarding on-premises data centers to DSPM provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Gain comprehensive visibility into data stored across all on-premises databases and systems.
- Improve your security posture of the databases.
- Have a unified view of data assets across hybrid environments (cloud and on-premise).
- Centralize risk assessment and management of on-premises databases.

Organizations can maintain consistent security policies and data protection measures across the hybrid infrastructure by integrating on-premises data centers with DSPM.

## About the On-Premises Data Centers Page

On the On-Premises Data Centers page (Policies > Common Configuration > DSPM > On-Premises Data Centers), you can do the following:

1. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables#filter) to view specific data.
2. [Add an on-premises data center to DSPM](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-premises-data-center).
3. View the list of on-premises data centers. For each on-premises data center, you can view:
  - **Account**: The name of the data center. Click to view the data center details.
    - Data Center Details
  - **Location**: The regions where the data centers are located.
  - **Business Unit**: The [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) assigned to the data center.
  - **Added By**: The user who added the data center.
  - **Added On**: The date and time the data center was added.
4. Sort the column data.
5. [Modify the table and its columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables#hide).
6. Click the **Action** icon to [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/editing-or-deleting-unmanaged-database) or [delete](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/editing-or-deleting-unmanaged-database) the data centers.

For each data center, you can:

1. [Edit the data center configuration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-premises-data-center).
2. [Delete the data center configuration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-premises-data-center).
3. **Data Center**: View the following information for the data center:
  - **Location**: The regions where the data centers are located.
  - **Business Unit**: The business unit assigned to the data center.
  - **Added On**: The date and time the data center was added.
  - **Added By**: The user who added the data center.
4. **Connected Scanners to the Data Center**: View the scanner connections configured for the data center:
  - **On-Premises Scanners Integration**: View a list of scanner integrations linked to the data center.

[Image: The On-Premises Data Center details page showing the configuration details and annotations on different sections]

[Image: The On-Premises Data Centers page with a list of data centers and annotations on different parts of the page.]

## About Data Classification Settings

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-classification-settings
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Data Classification Settings > About Data Classification Settings
- Last modified: 2026-07-08T22:00Z
- Summary: Information about the data sensitivity settings in the Zscaler Admin Console and how the DLP engines are used for data classification.

Sensitive data is confidential information such as personally identifiable information (PII), social security numbers, credit card information, financial data, login credentials, etc., that must be protected with strong security controls to prevent data breaches.

Knowing what type of sensitive data exists in your cloud environment and the resources where it is located is crucial to keep track and monitor this data regularly and ensure the data is secure. [Data classification](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-data-classification) is an effective method to classify sensitive data, as this enables you to evaluate the risks and take immediate action to protect sensitive data.

DSPM supports data classification by using robust [DLP engines and dictionaries](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-dlp-engines-and-dictionaries) that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA).

You can only view the DLP engines in the Zscaler Admin Console. You can modify a DLP engine in Internet & SaaS if you have the [necessary permissions](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-roles). When modifying a predefined or custom engine, you can also combine dictionaries with Boolean operators to create logical expressions.

Data classification includes the following benefits and enables you to:

- Classify sensitive data based on the level of sensitivity and risk.
- View the DLP engines and dictionaries that are used by DSPM for data classification.
- Manage the sensitivity settings for DLP engines.
- Enable or disable the DLP engine evaluation.

## About the Data Classification Settings Page

On the Data Classification Settings page (Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Data Classification Settings), you can do the following:

1. Modify DLP engines. This option is visible to users with permissions to view or edit the DLP Dictionaries & Engines page (Policies > Data Protection > Common Resources > DLP Dictionaries & Engines).
2. View the list of DLP engines that are synced from Internet & SaaS. For each DLP engine, you can view:
  1. **DLP Engine Name**: The name of the DLP engine.
  2. **Description**: The description of the DLP engine.
  3. **Engine Type**: The type (Predefined or Custom) of DLP engine.
  4. **Last Modified**: The date and time the DLP engine was last modified.
  5. **Enabled**: Whether the DLP engine evaluation is enabled or not.
  6. **Sensitive**: The data sensitivity setting (enabled or disabled) for the DLP engine. By default, the sensitivity setting is enabled for all DLP engines.
3. Sort the column data.
4. Enable or disable the DLP engine evaluation.
5. [Disable the sensitivity setting](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/disabling-sensitivity-setting-dlp-engines) for a specific DLP engine.
6. Search for a specific DLP engine.

[Image: View the list of DLP engines]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-data-duplications","lastmod":"2026-07-01T23:38Z","nid":"1529294"} -->
## About Data Duplications

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-duplications
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Data & Identity Inventory > About Data Duplications
- Last modified: 2026-07-01T23:38Z
- Summary: Information about the Data Duplication page, which shows scan results for detected duplicate files in data stores in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Data duplication refers to the presence of one or more identical copies of data, either intentionally or unintentionally, in different locations in an organization’s infrastructure. You can remove duplicate copies to reduce your attack surface, and track the source from where the sensitive data originated and its presence in different files.

DSPM scans the data stores and detects duplicate files across cloud, SaaS, and on-premises environments. This allows you to validate and delete the extra copies to limit the exposure of data to unauthorized users and protect sensitive data.

The Data Duplications page has the following benefits and enables you to:

- View all the duplicate copies of files and tables in the data stores.
- View DLP engines and dictionaries that were triggered to detect duplicate files and tables.
- Remove duplicate data to save on storage, backup, and operational costs.
- Reduce the possibility of users creating duplicate files.
- Delete potentially outdated data.

## About the Data Duplications Page

On the Data Duplications page (Analytics > Data Security > DSPM > Data Duplications), you can do the following:

1. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) to view specific information.
2. View the list of duplicate files. For each file copy you can see:
  - **File Path:** The location where the file exists. Click toview the details.
  - **Copies:** The total number of file copies detected, including the original file. Click the number to view the Duplications tab.
  - **DLP Engines** : The DLP engines that match the files.
  - **DLP Dictionaries:**The DLP dictionaries that match the files.
  - **Document Types:** The document type that matches the files.
  - **Hash:** The file’s MD5 sum.
  - **File Size:** The size of the file in kilobytes (KB).
  - **Total Size**: The total size of all the file copies.
  - **File Type:** The file type (e.g., txt).
  - **No. of Regions:** The number of regions where the duplicate file copies are found.
  - **No. of Accounts:** The number of cloud accounts in which duplicate file copies are found.
  - **Clouds:** The cloud service provider in which the duplicate file copies are found.
3. Export the data and [download the report](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/downloading-reports) as an Excel file by selecting one of the following options from the **Export**drop-down menu:
  - **Summary View**: This report is based on the current page view, including applied filters and visible columns. This report summarizes the total number of duplicate files and their locations across accounts and regions, identified by unique file hashes.
  - **Full View**: This report lists all duplicate file instances and their attributes. This report allows you to know the exact location of each duplicate file instance. The Full View report is generated as a ZIP file, which can contain up to 10 files with a maximum of 50,000 rows each. Use report filters to select and view specific data and stay within the 500,000-row limit.

- **Details**: The file properties.
- **Evidence**: Validate the findings and view trigger data along with the last scan. This tab is displayed only if [evidence collection option is enabled and configured](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-configuration) prior to the scan.
- **Data duplications**: Duplicate file copies. Click **File Path** to view the file details on the **Details**tab or click **Resource Name** to view the [resource inventory graph](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-resource-inventory-graph), [sensitive data](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-sensitive-data-details) available in the resource, or [alerts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alerts)generated for the resource.
- **File access**: The users that accessed the file in the last 7 days.

[Image: Shows duplicated files detected in your system.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-data-posture-policies","lastmod":"2026-04-21T21:06Z","nid":"1477751"} -->
## About Data Posture Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Data Posture Policies > About Data Posture Policies
- Last modified: 2026-04-21T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the data posture policies that are defined and implemented in DSPM.

[Watch a video about Data Posture Policies](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/iframe/pwx62y9unc) (shows legacy UI).

Data Posture policies are queries or rules that DSPM define to protect your cloud resources from potential threats and improve your cloud security posture. Policies provide guidelines for managing and protecting your organization's sensitive data and ensuring it is stored securely and only shared with authorized users.

DSPM scans the resources against the policies enabled in your Amazon Web Services (AWS) accounts, Azure subscriptions, and Google Cloud Storage; identifies where the sensitive data is located, vulnerabilities such as any misconfigurations, presence of malware, or if the resource is publicly exposed to the internet; and potential breach possibilities. DSPM generates [alerts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alerts) that help you prioritize an incident and quickly remediate the issue. The policies are grouped by [threat categories](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/threat-categories).

DSPM offers predefined policies that are aligned with industry standard cybersecurity and compliance benchmarks such as [NIST](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework), [GDPR](https://gdpr-info.eu/), [PCI](https://www.pcisecuritystandards.org/standards/), etc. You can create [custom policies](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/creating-custom-policies) to meet your organization's requirements. DSPM also provides predefined policies that use advanced options to scan the data.

Data Posture policies provide the following benefits and enable you to:

- View all the policies offered by DSPM.
- Gain data posture overview based on whether the policies are passing or failing for your resources.
- Create custom security policies to meet your organization's compliance requirements.
- Enable or disable policies on resources.

## About the Policies Page

On the Policy page (Policies > Data Protection > Policy > Data Posture Policies), you can do the following:

1. [Apply filters to view specific data](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
2. [Add additional filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
3. Search for a specific policy.
4. [Add a custom policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/creating-custom-policies).
5. View the policy details. For each policy, you can view:
  - **Policy Name**: The policy title.
  - **Severity**: The severity level (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) of the policy.
  - **Policy Source**: Whether the policy is a predefined or a custom policy.
  - **Primary Resource Type**: The type of resource on which the policy is applied.
    - List of supported resource types
  - **Last Updated**: The date and time the policy was last updated.
  - **Cloud**: The cloud type in which the resource is located.
  - **ID**: The unique identifier for the policy.
  - **Created**: The date and time the policy was created.
  - **Policy Category**: The category (Public Exposure, Data Loss, etc.) to which this policy belongs.
  - **Policy Status**: The status (Enabled or Disabled) of the policy.
6. Select multiple policies to either enable or disable them. See image.
7. Click the policy name to view additional details. To learn more, see [Viewing Policy Details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-policy-details).
8. Sort the column data.
9. View the list of policy categories associated with the policy.
10. [Enable or disable the policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-policies).
11. Select any of the following actions:
  - **Enable**: [Enable a policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-policies). This option is available only when the policy is disabled.
  - **Disable**: [Disable a policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-policies). This option is available only when the policy is enabled.
  - **Clone**: [Clone a policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-policies).
  - **Change Severity**: Change the severity level of the policy.
  - **Edit**: [Edit a custom policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-policies).
  - **Delete**: [Delete a custom policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-policies). You cannot edit, delete, or change the severity level for predefined policies.
12. [Show or hide the columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).

[Image: The list of policies and various actions that can be performed on them.]

[Image: Enable or disable multiple policies simultaneously]

- EC2 Instance
- RDS Cluster
- RDS Instance
- S3 Bucket
- SQL Server
- Storage Account
- Virtual Machine

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-evidence-settings","lastmod":"2026-07-02T07:06Z","nid":"1540684"} -->
## About Evidence Settings

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-evidence-settings
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > On-Premises Data Centers and Scanners > Evidence > About Evidence Settings
- Last modified: 2026-07-02T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about evidence configuration for on-premises scanning in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Evidence is the data captured when sensitive information is discovered during an on-premises scan. Evidence collection is a feature in DSPM to capture and store evidence of sensitive information found during [on-premises scanning](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-premises-scanner-integrations). The data snippets are stored directly in your organization's cloud storage (e.g., AWS S3 bucket) and are not stored in the Zscaler infrastructure, maintaining compliance with data privacy and security.

Evidence configuration is linked to specific [on-premises data centers](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-center). Sensitive data detected by the on-premises scanner is uploaded to the configured cloud storage via DSPM.

You can choose how to provision the cloud storage:

- **Zscaler Managed**: DSPM automatically creates and manages a storage bucket in your cloud account. This is the recommended option for a simple setup.
- **Custom**: You provide an existing S3 bucket that is already configured in your organization's cloud account.

Configuring evidence settings provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Store sensitive data on your cloud infrastructure.
- Protect data with end-to-end encryption throughout the entire workflow, from scanning to storage.
- Route the evidence data through the existing DSPM service connection and eliminate the need to open the on-premises scanner network to external cloud storage IP addresses.
- Provide security analysts with proof of sensitive data discovery to expedite remediation.
- Centralize evidence rules for multiple on-premises data centers in a single view.

## About the Evidence Settings Page

On the Evidence Settings page (Policies > Common Configuration > DSPM > Evidence Settings), you can do the following:

1. Search for specific rules using the rule name.
2. [Modify the table and its columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables#hide).
3. [Add a new evidence rule](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-evidence-rule).
4. View the list of configured evidence rules. For each rule, you can view the following details:
  - **Rule Name**: The name assigned to the evidence rule during configuration.
    - Evidence Rule Details
  - **Datastore**: The type of data store associated with the evidence rule.
  - **Cloud**: The public cloud provider hosting the evidence storage.
  - **Storage Type**: Indicates whether the storage is Zscaler managed or a custom (provided by the customer).
  - **Connection Status**: The [validation](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#validate-evidence-rule) status (Success, Failed, Pending) of the evidence rule.
  - **Error**: The error message indicating why the [evidence rule validation](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#validate-evidence-rule) failed.
  - **Enable/Disable**: Indicates whether the evidence rule is active. Toggle to [enable](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#enablingdisabling-rule) or [disable](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#enablingdisabling-rule) the rule.
  - **Added By**: The user who added the evidence rule.
  - **Added On**: The date and time the evidence rule was added.
5. [Sort the column data](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables#sort).
6. Use the **Actions** icon to [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#edit-evidence-rule), [validate](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#validate-evidence-rule), or [delete](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#delete-evidence-rule) the rule configuration.

[Image: The evidence settings page with a list of evidence rules configured and annotations on different parts of the page.]

For each evidence rule, you can view the following details:

1. Action menu to [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#edit-evidence-rule), [validate](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#validate-evidence-rule), or [delete](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules#delete-evidence-rule) the evidence rule configuration.
2. **Evidence**:
  - **Rule Name**: The name assigned to the evidence rule during configuration.
  - **Cloud Type**: The public cloud provider hosting the evidence storage.
  - **S3 Bucket Name** (or equivalent): The name of the storage bucket or container where the evidence snippets are stored.
  - **Storage Type**: Indicates if the storage is Zscaler managed (provisioned by DSPM) or a custom (provided by the customer).
  - **S3 Bucket Account ID**: The identifier of the cloud account where the evidence storage bucket is located.
  - **KMS Key ARN** (Custom Storage): The identifier for your encryption key, ensuring data at rest is protected by your organization's security policies.
  - **Data Centers**: The list of data centers associated with this rule. Any scanner assigned to these data centers uses this rule for evidence uploads.
  - **IAM Role**: The IAM role (e.g., z-dspm-evidence-role) created in your cloud environment. This role grants the scanner permission to upload findings and the Zscaler Admin Console permission to read them.
3. **Download Template**:
  - **CloudFormation**: Download [CloudFormation template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization#cloudform-template-prereq) to automate the provisioning of the required IAM roles and policies.
  - **Terraform**: Download [Terraform template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization#terraform-template-prereq) for managing your infrastructure configuration.

[Image: Details of an individual evidence rule configuration]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-identity-inventory","lastmod":"2026-07-02T02:13Z","nid":"1529532"} -->
## About Identity Inventory

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-identity-inventory
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Data & Identity Inventory > About Identity Inventory
- Last modified: 2026-07-02T02:13Z
- Summary: Information about the Identity Inventory, which lists all identities within the cloud environment, along with details about the type and number of data stores that a user has access to.

An identity represents a user, device, application, or service that can access data stores containing sensitive data in the cloud environment. While securing sensitive data, it is crucial to control and manage the permissions assigned to identities, as excessive permissions and insecure configurations could lead to security breaches. DSPM detects identities in all the onboarded cloud accounts (AWS, Azure, and GCP), including [managed and unmanaged databases, and Snowflake.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-graph-databases)

Identity Inventory has the following benefits and enables you to:

- View the identities that can access resources containing sensitive data within your cloud environment.
- View the data stores accessed by an identity.
- View the type of sensitive data accessed by each identity.
- View the security posture of the identity.

## About the Identity Inventory Page

On the Identity Inventory page (Analytics > Data Security > DSPM > Identity Inventory), you can do the following:

1. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) to view specific data.
2. Apply additional filters.
3. Search for specific data in the searchable columns.
4. View the list of identities. For each identity, you can see:
  - **Entity Name**: The name of the entity. Click to view additional details in a drawer.
  - **Entity ID**: The unique identifier of the identity.
  - **Entity Type**: The type of the identity (AWS Account, IAM Unmanaged User, etc.).
  - **Entity Source**: The identity repository (e.g., Entra ID) where the identity is stored.
  - **Entity Category**: The identity category (e.g., services, users, external, services, applications, managed identities, roles, federated, admin principals).
  - **Target Environment**: The cloud service providers (e.g., GCP, Azure) to which the identity has access.
  - **Cloud**: The cloud service provider in which the identity is present.
  - **Posture**: The security posture assigned to the identity (Dormant Identity, MFA Disabled, etc.). Hover over the label to see the description of each posture.
  - **Data Stores**: The number of data stores that the identity has access to.
  - **Sensitive Data Stores**: The number of data stores containing sensitive data.
  - **Triggers**: The total number of records that matched the DLP engines.
  - **Files & Tables**: The number of files and tables the identity has access to.
  - **DLP Engines**: The DLP engines in the data stores.
  - **DLP Dictionaries**: The DLP dictionaries associated with the DLP Engines.
  - **Document Categories**: The document category to which the document type belongs.
5. View the posture assigned to the identity.
6. View the list of DLP engines that the identity has access to. See image.
7. View the list of document categories. See image.
8. Export the results and [download the report](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/downloading-reports)as an Excel file.
9. [Show or hide columns in the table.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)

[Image: Shows the list of DLP engines that matched the data stores]

[Image: Shows the list of document categories that matched the data stores]

[Image: Shows additional details about identities]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-ignore-alert-filters","lastmod":"2026-04-15T00:36Z","nid":"1477816"} -->
## About Ignore Alert Filters

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-ignore-alert-filters
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Alerts > Ignore Alert Filters > About Ignore Alert Filters
- Last modified: 2026-04-15T00:36Z
- Summary: Information about DSPM ignore alert filters in the Zscaler Admin Console.

The ignore alert filter allows you to exclude the generation of alerts for less critical violations. By adding an ignore alert filter, you can avoid receiving notifications or taking actions on such policy violations. When you add an ignore alert filter, DSPM stops generating alerts for the selected filter scope, and notifications aren't sent to any [third-party integrations](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-third-party-integrations). This allows you to focus on critical alerts and prioritize them. For example, you can add an ignore alert filter to exclude alerts that are generated for [policies](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies)with low severity or for a specific [cloud account](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts).

The ignore alert filter provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Ignore alerts that you do not want to be notified for or take action on.
- Reduce the number of alerts in the Zscaler Admin Console.
- Focus on critical alerts.

## About the Ignore Alert Filter Page

On the Ignore Alert Filter page (Administration > Alerts > Ignore Alert Filter), you can do the following:

1. [Add an ignore alert filter.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-ignore-filters)
2. View the list of ignore alert filters. For each filter, you can see:
  - **Alert Filter Name**: The name of the ignore alert filter. Click to view additional details. You can also edit, delete, enable, or disable the filter. See image.
  - **Filter Scope**: The scope ([business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units), [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies), tags, etc.) selected for the ignore alert filter. If the selected scope is deleted (e.g., policies are deleted, accounts are offboarded, or the business unit is deleted), the ignore alert filter is disabled, and an exclamation mark is displayed indicating the alert filter is invalid. See image.; Click the alert filter name to see the reason why the ignore alert filter is disabled. See image.; You can enable the filter only after at least one filter scope is available.; If multiple policies, accounts, or resource types are selected for the filter scope and only one of them is deleted, the ignore alert filter is not impacted.
  - **Created By**: The user who created the filter.
  - **Created Date**: The date and time the filter was created.
  - **Updated By**: The user who updated the filter.
  - **Last Updated**: The date and time the filter was updated.
3. Search for a specific ignore alert filter.
4. [Modify the table and its columns.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
5. [Enable or disable the ignore alert filter.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-ignore-alert-filters) By default, the ignore alert filter is enabled.
6. [Edit or delete the ignore alert filter.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-ignore-alert-filters)

[Image: The Actions drop-down menu with the list of actions available.]

[Image: The Ignore Alert Filter page with annotation around invalid alert filter.]

[Image: The ignore alert filter drawer displaying the general information of the filter.]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/about-investigation","lastmod":"2026-04-24T21:06Z","nid":"1477766"} -->
## About Investigation

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-investigation
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Investigation > About Investigation
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T21:06Z
- Summary: Information about the investigation feature in DSPM.

[Watch a video on Investigation with DSPM](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/iframe/my630v87t6) (shows legacy UI).

Your cloud resources containing data might be located in different regions. Depending on the number of cloud accounts you have onboarded, DSPM offers insights by identifying sensitive data, vulnerabilities, or any other risks in your resources.

You might want to obtain certain information related to the security posture of your cloud resources without having to create alerts or filter information on the dashboard. For example, you want to look at all S3 buckets that were scanned in the past week and check what type of sensitive data is stored in these S3 buckets. You can leverage DSPM's Investigation feature to effectively parse such information, and based on the result, save the investigation or create a custom security policy.

The Investigation feature provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Run queries on cloud resources and gain more insight into the security posture of your data.
- Customize queries, run them multiple times, inspect results, and then discard or save the queries, either as investigation queries or custom security policies.

## About the Investigation Page

On the Investigation page (Logs > Insights > Investigation), you can do the following:

1. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) to view specific information.
2. [Add a new investigation](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/creating-new-investigation).
3. View the investigation queries that you've created. For each investigation, you can see:
  - **Cloud**: The name of the cloud service provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
  - **Query**: The query string.
  - **Resource Type**: The type of resource on which the query is run.
4. View the list of saved investigation queries.
5. Search for a query in the searchable columns.
6. [Show or hide columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables).
7. Click the **Actions** icon to run, save, or [edit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/editing-or-deleting-investigation) a query. When you run a query, the investigation results are displayed. See image. Click the resource name to view the [resource details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-resource-details).

[Image: Create a new investigation and view the previously created queries]

[Image: Investigation query results for an EC2 instance]

## About On-Premises Scanner Integrations

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-premises-scanner-integrations
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > On-Premises Data Centers and Scanners > On-Premises Scanners > About On-Premises Scanner Integrations
- Last modified: 2026-05-17T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about on-premises scanner integrations in the Zscaler Admin Console.

DSPM provides support to integrate the on-premises scanners deployed in your organization's network and use them to scan the data stored in on-premises systems such as file servers and unmanaged resources. On-premesis scanners provide direct access to internal data sources, enabling granular visibility into sensitive data and maintain the data security posture across hybrid environments by extending scanning capabilities to internal systems.

Integrating on-premises scanners with DSPM provides the following benefits and enables you to:

- Gain visibility into sensitive data stored in on-premises environments.
- Strengthen the security posture of the internal infrastructure.
- Maintain consistent data protection policies across on-premises environments.
- Detect misconfigurations, vulnerabilities, and potential threats that could lead to data exposure.
- Respond to security risks and take corrective actions to prevent data breaches.

## System Requirements

For optimal DSPM scanner performance, ensure the following system requirements are met:

- Virtual Machine
- Network Requirements
- Supported File Server Protocols

| Component | Minimum Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU | 16 Virtual Cores | Intel Xeon or AMD EPYC, or the latest. ARM processors are not supported. |
| RAM | 32 GB | Dedicated memory for the VM. |
| Storage | 100 GB SSD | High-performance storage is crucial for efficient scanning. |
| Operating System | Embedded within OVA (Ubuntu 22.04) | The image includes the OS; no separate license is required. |

The DSPM scanner for on-premises file servers requires specific network configurations to operate correctly and securely.

| Component | Requirement | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Network Interface | 10 Gigabit Ethernet (GbE) | Dedicated to the VM. Wired connection preferred. |
| IP Addressing | Static IP Address | For consistent connectivity and management. |
| DNS Resolution | To resolve internal and external hosts | Required for communication with file servers and cloud services. |
| **Firewall Rules (Outbound)** |  |  |
| Port 443 (HTTPS) | To DSPM Cloud Management Platform | For updates and configuration synchronization. |
| Port 445 (SMB) | To SMB File Servers | For scanning SMB file shares. |
| Port 2049 (NFS) | To NFS File Servers | For scanning NFS file shares. |
| Port 53 (DNS) | To DNS Server | For DNS resolution. |
| Port 88 (Kerberos) | To Kerberos | For Kerberos authentication. |
| Port 111 (NFS) | To NFS File Servers | For NFS Portmapper. |

The on‑premises file‑server scanning solution supports the following protocol versions for scanning file servers:

| Protocol | Versions | Details |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SMB | 2.0, 2.1, 3.0, 3.02, 3.1.1 | Required for scanning Windows file shares. |
| NFS | v4.0, v4.1, v4.2 | Required for scanning Linux/Windows shares. |

## About the On-Premises Scanner Integrations Page

On the On-Premises Scanner Integrations page (Policies > Common Configuration > DSPM > On-Premises Scanners), you can do the following:

1. [Add an on-premises scanner to DSPM](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-premises-scanner-integration).
2. View the list of on-premises scanner integrations. For each scanner integration, you can view:
  - **Integration**: The name assigned to the scanner integration. Click the integration name to see the following details:
    - Scanner Integration Details
  - **Scanner**: The scanner instance name.
  - **Version**: The version of the scanner software.
  - **IP Address**: The IP address of the scanner.
  - **Scanner Status**: Whether the scanner is operational or pending.
  - **Last Connected On**: The last time the on-premises scanner instance was successfully connected with DSPM.
  - **Added On**: The date and time the scanner was added to DSPM.
  - **Added By**: The user who added the scanner.
3. Sort the column data.
4. [Modify the table and its columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables#hide).
5. [Delete](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-premises-scanner-integration#delete) the scanner integration.

1. **General Information**:
  - **Scanner**: The scanner instance name.
  - **Version**: The version of the scanner software.
  - **IP Address**: The IP address of the scanner.
  - **Status**: Whether the scanner is operational or not.
  - **Added On**: The date and time the scanner was added to DSPM.
  - **Added By**: The user who added the scanner.
2. **API Key Management**:
  - **API Key**: The key used to authenticate the scanner.
  - **Regenerate Key**: Click to generate a new API key when the key is compromised, exceeds your rotation threshold, or you need to rotate credentials per policy.
3. **Scanner Image Download**:
  - **Select Virtualization Platform**: Choose the platform on which the DSPM scanner image must be downloaded (i.e., **VMware** or **Hyper-V**).
  - Name and format of the scanner image: OVA for VMware and VHD for Hyper-V.
  - **Checksum**: The checksum value for image verification.
  - **Size**: The file size of the scanner image.
  - **Download Scanner Image**: Click to download the image file.
4. **Data Center Association**: Download and install the scanner image to scan and monitor data stored within the on-premises data center. To learn more, see [Adding On-Premises Scanner Integration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-premises-scanner-integration).
5. [Delete the scanner integration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-premises-scanner-integration#delete).

[Image: Scanner integration details showing, status operational, and API key information.]

[Image: The On-Premises Scanner Integration page with a list of scanners and annotations on different parts of the page.]

## About Resource Inventory

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-resource-inventory
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Resource Inventory > About Resource Inventory
- Last modified: 2026-07-02T02:36Z
- Summary: Information about the Resource Inventory page in the Zscaler Admin Console

Sensitive data such as personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), financial records, social security number, etc., are confidential and valuable information that must be protected and kept secure at all times. Not knowing where the sensitive data is stored or not protecting this data is a huge risk, which could lead to data breaches such as hackers accessing valuable data and exploiting the vulnerabilities in the system. In addition, it could also lead to financial and compliance issues. Therefore, it is crucial to know where your sensitive data is stored within your cloud environment, so you can implement strong security controls to keep the data secure.

DSPM [scans your cloud resources](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings) or data stores for sensitive data and vulnerabilities and displays the scan results on the Resource Inventory page. You can view the list of resources containing sensitive data, the cloud accounts in which the resources are stored, regions where these accounts are located, severity of risk associated with the resources, different types of sensitive data, security posture, the predefined [DLP engines and dictionaries](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-dlp-engines-and-dictionaries) that match the sensitive records, document types, scan schedule, and much more. You can also export this data and download the report as an Excel file.

The data scan results are also displayed as [graphs](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-data-inventory-graph) that visually represent the resources and sensitive data stored in them, including the [public exposure path](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-public-exposure-path) and [user access path](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-user-access-path).

The Resource Inventory has the following benefits and enables you to:

- View the scan results for the resources.
- View the type of sensitive data stored in the resources.
- View the vulnerabilities detected in the primary and associated resources.
- Gain insight into the malware detected in the resources.
- Know the geographic location of the resource.
- View the severity of risk associated with the resource containing sensitive data.
- View the security posture of the resource.
- View the IAM entities that can access the resource.
- View the different types of documents classified by categories, which are present in the data stores.
- Take immediate action to resolve the issues and protect your sensitive data.

## About the Resource Inventory Page

On the Resource Inventory page (Analytics > Data Security > DSPM > Resource Inventory), you can do the following:

1. Apply [filters](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) to view specific data.
2. Use additional filters.
3. Search for specific data in the searchable columns.
4. View the list of resources. For each resource, you can see:
  - **Resource Name**: The name of the cloud resource.
  - **Resource ID**: The unique identifier of the cloud resource.
  - **Cloud Account**: The unique identifier for the cloud account that contains this resource.
  - **Account ID**: The unique identifier of the cloud account.
  - **Business Unit**: The [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) to which the account belongs.
  - **Risk Level**: The severity of the risk (Critical, High, Medium, or Low) associated with the resource.
  - **Posture**: The security posture (publicly exposed, no logging, etc.) of the resource. Hover over the label to see the description for each posture. To learn more, see [Understanding the Security Posture State](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-security-posture-state). See image.
  - **Malware**: Malware detected in the resources.
  - **DLP Engines**: The number of sensitive records that match the DLP engine.
  - **DLP Dictionaries**: The number of sensitive records that match the dictionaries.
  - **Document Categories**: The different document categories to which the documents belong.
  - **Document Types**: The different types of documents detected by [machine learning (ML)-based DLP dictionaries](https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-predefined-dlp-dictionaries). See image.
  - **Open Alerts**: The number of [alerts](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-alert-details) in Open state.
  - **Region**: The region where the resource is located.
  - **First Discovered**: The date and time the resource was first detected.
  - **Data Scanned**: The size of the scanned data.
  - **Last Completed Scan**: The date and time the resource was last scanned.
  - **Latest Scan Status**: The latest scan status indicates the state of the scanning process. To learn more, see [Understanding Scan Status](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-scan-status). For failed or unsupported scans, hover over the **Failed**or **Unsupported**labels to see the error message. The error message contains the timestamp to indicate when the error occurred, resource ID, and error reason. Click the **Copy** icon to copy the resource ID. See image.
5. Click the [Resource Name](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-resource-details) to view additional details about the resource.
6. View the security posture of the resource. See image.
7. View the malware details.
8. View the list of DLP engines that match the sensitive records. See image.
9. View the list of DLP dictionaries included in the DLP engine. See image.
10. Export the results and [download the report](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-reports) as an Excel file. If you are unable to view all the records in the downloaded report, Zscaler recommends you apply relevant filters before exporting.
11. [Show or hide columns](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables) in the table.
12. Save the current page setting as a new page view.

[Image: View the list of resources containing sensitive data]

[Image: The DLP engines that match the sensitive records]

[Image: The list of DLP dictionaries that match the sensitive ecords]

[Image: The document types that are stored in the resource]

[Image: The different security posture labels applied to the resource]

[Image: The details of the security posture applied to the resource]

[Image: The reason why the scan failed]

Apply filters, select the required columns, and save this page setting so you can see the same view every time you visit the page.

To save a page view:

1. Click **Default View** in the top right corner and select **Save as New View**. See image.
2. In the **Save View** window:
  1. **View Name**: Enter the name for this page setting.
  2. **Description**(Optional): Enter a description.
3. Select the **Set as default view** checkbox to set this view as default. See image.
4. Click **Save**.

You can save multiple page views and delete a view as required.

[Image: Select the Save as New View option]

[Image: Save the page view]

## About SaaS Applications

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-saas-applications
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > SaaS Applications > About SaaS Applications
- Last modified: 2026-07-28T08:34Z
- Summary: Information about SaaS applications in the Zscaler Admin Console.

DSPM provides visibility and security for SaaS applications used in your organizations. You can integrate application tenants with DSPM to monitor and scan the data stores within the SaaS applications, apply the Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) labels to on-premises Azure file shares, or integrate with Microsoft Copilot.

Support for scanning SaaS applications provides the following key benefits and allows you to:

- Detect sensitive data, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities in data stores.
- Apply the Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) labels.
- Integrate with Microsoft Copilot.

## About the SaaS Applications Page

On the SaaS Applications page (Policies > Common Configuration > DSPM>SaaS Applications), you can do the following:

1. [Add an M365 tenant.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-365-tenant)
2. View the list of all configured SaaS tenants. For each tenant, you can see:
  - **Tenant Name**: The name of the SaaS tenant.
  - **Tenant ID**: The ID of the SaaS tenant.
  - **Authentication Mode**: The authentication type (e.g., **Client Secret**, **Certificate**) selected for the tenant.
  - **Status**: The status of the onboarded tenant.
    - **Successfully Configured**: The tenant is configured and validated successfully.
    - **Needs Attention**: The tenant configuration has failed (e.g., invalid client secret or certificate).
  - **Status Details**: The details of the status. This is available only for tenants with the Needs Attention status.
  - **Last Validated**: The last time the SaaS tenant was validated.
  - **Added On**: The date and time the SaaS tenant was added.
  - **Added By**: The user who onboarded the tenant.
3. [Modify the table and its columns.](https://help.zscaler.com/unified/using-tables)
4. [Edit or delete a tenant.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-saas-application-tenants)

[Image: The SaaS Applications page with the list of configured SaaS tenants.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->
