<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/adding-organization-details","lastmod":"2026-07-01T23:45Z","nid":"1525716"} -->
## Adding Organization Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-organization-details
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Adding Organization Details
- Last modified: 2026-07-01T23:45Z
- Summary: Information about adding AWS organization details in the Zscaler Admin Console.

The first step in the [onboarding process](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization) is to provide the AWS organization details in the Zscaler Admin Console. DSPM uses these details to generate a template to connect to the AWS organization.

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Click **Add New**.
3. In the **Select Cloud Provider** window: See image.
  - For **Select Cloud Type**, select **AWS**.
  - For **Select Onboarding Type**, select **Organization**.
4. Click **Next**.
5. In the **Add New Organization Configuration** section: See image.
  - **Organization Details**: Provide the AWS organization details.
    - **DSPM Alias**: Enter a user-friendly name for the organization that you want to onboard.
    - **Role Name**: Enter a unique role name. This role name is added as a prefix to all the [roles](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/iam-roles-and-permissions-aws) that are created during the onboarding process.
    - **Management Account Name**: Enter the name of the management account. You can find this in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) under **Organization**.
    - **Management Account ID**: Enter the 12-digit AWS account ID of the management account.
    - **Organization ID**: Enter the organization ID that you want to onboard. You can find this in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) in multiple ways. For example:
      1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
      2. On the top right, select your account and then click **Organization**.
      3. In the left-side navigation, copy the **Organization ID**. See image.
    - **Notification Emails** (Optional): Enter the email addresses of the recipients who must be notified of any configuration or permissions issues encountered with the onboarded organization. You can add up to 30 email addresses of recipients. You can also add email addresses after completing the onboarding process.
    - **External ID**: View the optional identifier that is autopopulated. This ID is used in an IAM role trust policy to designate a specific user to assume the IAM role to provide access to the AWS resources. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_create_for-user_externalid.html).
  - **Configure CloudTrail Integration (Optional)**: Select the checkbox to provide CloudTrail details. When enabled, DSPM gains read-only access to the CloudTrail logs required for [incremental scans](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-aws-cloud-storage) on the S3 bucket. When disabled, DSPM supports only full scans. See image.
    - **CloudTrail Type**: Select the **OrgCloudTrail** checkbox, if it is an organization CloudTrail. [Organization CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-aws-cloudtrail) shares the CloudTrail events of the management and member accounts of the organization to the same CloudTrail S3 bucket. During initial onboarding, DSPM checks for log files to perform data scan in the following paths: After the onboarding is completed successfully, DSPM checks for log files in each target account.
      | CloudTrail Type | Path |
      | --- | --- |
      | Organization CloudTrail | `prefix/<organization ID>/<management account ID>` |
      | Account CloudTrail | `prefix/<management account ID>` |
    - **CloudTrail Bucket Name**: Enter the S3 bucket name that is associated with CloudTrail. This S3 bucket stores the CloudTrail events.
    - **Prefix**: Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail S3 bucket path. If your CloudTrail is part of the AWS Control Tower, enter the organization ID as prefix. You can find this on the **Trails**page, under the **Log file prefix**column in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/). See image.
    - **Bucket Account ID**: Enter the 12-digit AWS account ID where CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.
6. Click **Apply**to continue. Click **Reset** if you want to change the details.

If all the details are accurate, you are directed to the [Connect to the Organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/deploy-aws-tree-discovery-template) section to deploy the tree discovery template.

[Image: The Trails page in the AWS Management Console with annotation around organization ID in the Log file prefix column.]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/adding-premises-file-servers","lastmod":"2026-07-02T07:06Z","nid":"1532037"} -->
## Adding an On-Premises File Server

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-premises-file-servers
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Service Registration > On-Premises File Servers > Adding an On-Premises File Server
- Last modified: 2026-07-02T07:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to add an on-premises file servers in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can add an [on-premises file servers](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-service-registration) to DSPM. DSPM scans the data assets for sensitive data and identifies any potential security posture risks.

## Prerequisites

Before adding an on-premises file server to DSPM, ensure the following prerequisites are met:

- Integrate an on-premises scanner with DSPM to enable scanning of on-premises file servers. To learn more, see [Adding or Deleting a Scanner Integration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-premises-scanner-integration).
- Create an on-premises data center and associate it with the configured on-premises scanner. To learn more, see [Adding an On-Premises Data Center](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-premises-data-center).
- Configure the Network File System (NFS) client on the scanner host before you add NFS-based file servers. To learn more, see [Configuring the NFS Client](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-nfs-client).
- Add a Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) server for DSPM to map identities to file share entitlements. To learn more, see [Adding an LDAP Server](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-ldap-server).

## Adding an On-Premises File Server

To add an on-premises file server:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Service Registration**.
2. On the **Service Registration** page, select the **On-Premises File Servers** tab, and click **Add File Server**. See image. The **Add On-Premises File Server** drawer appears.
3. In the **Add On-Premises File Server** drawer: See image.
  1. **File Server Information**:
    1. **File Server Name**: Enter a unique name for the file server.
    2. **Protocol**: Select the communication protocol used to connect to the file server.
    3. **Version**(available only if **NFS** protocol is selected): Select the NFS version to use.
    4. **File Server Type**: Select the file server OS type.
      - **NFS**: Select **Windows**, **Linux**, or **NetApp**.
      - **SMB**: Select **Windows**, or **NetApp**.
  2. **Connection Attributes**:
    1. **File Server IP / Hostname**: Enter the IP address or hostname of the file server. For an NFS protocol and NetApp file server type, enter the hostname only.
    2. **Domain Name**: Enter the domain name associated with the file server.
    3. **Port**: Select the port used for communication protocol.
      - **Default Port**: SMB uses `445` and NFS uses `2049`.
      - **Custom Port**: Enter a valid port number based on your configuration requirements.
  3. **Authentication**: The authentication fields available depend on the **Protocol** and **File Server Type** selected. The following table lists the availability of each field based on the selected protocol and file server type:
    - **Secret Provider Type**: This field is autopopulated with the provider used to manage authentication secrets, typically set to Zscaler DSPM.
    - **Authentication Type**: Select the authentication method used to access file shares:
      - **Kerberos**: Uses Kerberos-based authentication to access file shares.
      - **AUTH_SYS**: Uses system-level User Identifier (UID) or Group Identifier (GID) credentials for authentication.
      - **NTLMv2**: Uses NT LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication to access file shares.
    - **Username**: Enter the username used to authenticate access to the file server.
    - **Password**: Enter the password associated with the username.
    - **Group IDs**: Enter one or more GIDs that have access to the file share, separated by commas.
    | Field | Availability |
    | --- | --- |
    | Authentication Type | Available only when NetApp is selected as the file server type. |
    | Kerberos | Available for NFS or SMB protocol with NetApp file server type. |
    | AUTH_SYS | Available for NFS protocol with NetApp file server type only. |
    | NTLMv2 | Available for SMB protocol with NetApp file server type only. |
    | Username | Available for Windows or Linux file server types, or when Kerberos or NTLMv2 is selected for NetApp. |
    | Password | Available for Windows or Linux file server types, or when Kerberos or NTLMv2 is selected for NetApp. |
    | Group IDs | Available only when AUTH_SYS is selected as the Authentication Type. |
  4. **LDAP Server** (available only when **SMB** is selected as the protocol):
    - **Server (Optional)**: Select the registered LDAP server for the on-premises file server.
  5. **Data Center Association**:
    1. **Data Center**: Select the [data center](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-center) where the file server is located.
    2. **Location**: This field is autopopulated based on the data center selection.
4. Click **Save**. The **Add On-Premises File Server** confirmation window appears.
5. In the**Add On-Premises File Server** confirmation window, read the message, and then click **Confirm and Save**. See image.

The on-premises file server is added and appears in the list on the **On-Premises File Servers** tab on the [Service Registration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-service-registration) page. DSPM starts to discover the file servers. If the discovery process fails, an error message is displayed in the [Error](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-service-registration#on-prem-tab) column.

To configure the scan settings, see [Configuring Scan Rule for](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[On-P](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[r](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[em](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[is](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[es](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[File Se](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[r](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[v](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[e](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers)[rs](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-premises-file-servers).

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/adding-snowflake-database-account","lastmod":"2026-06-22T02:36Z","nid":"1529987"} -->
## Adding a Snowflake Database Account

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-snowflake-database-account
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Service Registration > Snowflake > Adding a Snowflake Database Account
- Last modified: 2026-06-22T02:36Z
- Summary: Information on how to add a Snowflake account in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can add a [Snowflake account](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-service-registration) to DSPM. DSPM scans the Snowflake databases for sensitive data and identifies any potential security posture risks.

## Prerequisites

Before adding a Snowflake account to DSPM, ensure the following prerequisites are met:

- 1. Create a warehouse for DSPM.
- 2. Create a role with required permissions.
- 3. Create a user for DSPM.
- 4. Configure network policy for the DSPM user.
- 5. Provide SQL connection strings and authentication credentials to allow DSPM to access the Snowflake account.
- 6. Set up the secrets in the same environment as the DSPM orchestrator.

- **AWS**: Create and store the password or key‑pair in AWS Secrets Manager in the AWS account where the orchestrator account is present, and have the ARNs ready for use.
  1. Open the **AWS Secrets Manager** in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
  2. Select **Store a new secret**.
  3. On the **Choose secret type** page: See image.
    1. **Secret type**: Select **Other type of secret**.
    2. **Key/value pairs**: Select the **Plaintext** tab and enter the generated secret.
  4. Click **Next**.
  5. On the **Configure secret** page: See image
    1. **Secret name**: Enter a name for the secret.
    2. **Description** (optional): Enter a description if required.
  6. Click **Next**.
  7. On the **Configure rotation** page, click **Next**.
  8. On the **Review** page, review your secret details, and then click **Store**. See image.
- **Azure**: Create and store the secret in the Azure Key Vault of the worker plane resource group in the subscription where the orchestrator account is present, and have the Key Vault URIs ready for use. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/secrets/quick-create-portal).
- **GCP**: Create and store the secret in Secret Manager in the GCP project where the orchestrator account is present, and have the Secret ID paths ready for use. To learn more, refer to the [GCP documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/creating-and-accessing-secrets).

[Image: Review secret details window to verify the secret details]

[Image: Configure secret window to configure the name of the secret.]

[Image: AWS Secret Manager window showing options to store new secrets.]

When deploying DSPM components in Azure, a specific configuration is required to ensure secure communication with Snowflake. Use the Azure CLI to create a private key and secret, as the Azure portal does not support multiple inputs for secrets.

```
az keyvault secret set --vault-name snowflakekeyvaultvikas --name azuremultilinersakey --file "<filepath>"
```

Network policy allows communication between the DSPM components deployed in the customer scanner account and Snowflake.

1. Get the public IP address of the NAT that will be used to perform the data scan.
2. Create a network rule in Snowflake to allow ingress traffic from the NAT public IP: `CREATE NETWORK RULE ALLOW_INGRESS_ZSCALER_POLICY MODE = 'INGRESS' TYPE = 'IPV4' VALUE_LIST = ('xx.xx.xx.xx');`If you need to modify or update an existing network rule to include additional IP addresses: `ALTER NETWORK RULE ALLOW_INGRESS_ZSCALER_POLICY SET VALUE_LIST = ('xx.xxx.xx.xxx', 'xx.xx.xxx.xxx','xxx.xx.xxx.xx/xx');`
3. After the network rule is created, create a network with allowed network rule: `CREATE NETWORK POLICY ALLOW_INGRESS_ZSCALER_POLICY ALLOWED_NETWORK_RULE_LIST = ('ALLOW_INGRESS_ZSCALER_POLICY');`
4. Attach the created network policy to the user: `ALTER USER dspmdatascanuser SET NETWORK_POLICY = ALLOW_INGRESS_ZSCALER_POLICY;`

Choose any of the two options to create and authenticate a user for DSPM:

- Basic Authentication (Using PAT)
- Private Key Authentication

After the user is created, verify that the default warehouse and role are set correctly.

See image.

[Image: Snowflake Edit User window displaying the fields such as login name, display name, default role, and default warehouse.]

1. Create a private key using either an unencrypted or encrypted format:
  - Unencrypted key (without passphrase) `openssl genrsa 2048 | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -inform PEM -out rsa_key.p8 -nocrypt`
  - Encrypted key (with passphrase) `openssl genrsa 2048 | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -v2 des3 -inform PEM -out rsa_key.p8`
2. Use the generated private key to create a corresponding public key: `openssl rsa -in rsa_key.p8 -pubout -out rsa_key.pub`
3. Create the user account in Snowflake using the public key: `CREATE USER dspmdatascanuser DEFAULT_ROLE = "dspmdatascanrole" DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE = "dspmwarehouse" RSA_PUBLIC_KEY="<rsa_public_key>";`
4. Assign the role to the user: `GRANT ROLE dspmdatascanrole TO USER dspmdatascanuser;`
5. Store the private key in the scanner account's secret manager for DSPM authentication.

1. Create a user account in Snowflake with default configurations: `CREATE USER dspmdatascanuser DEFAULT_ROLE = "dspmdatascanrole" DEFAULT_WAREHOUSE = "dspmwarehouse";`
2. Assign the role to the user: `GRANT ROLE dspmdatascanrole TO USER dspmdatascanuser;`
3. Generate a programmatic access token (PAT) for this newly created user from the Snowflake UI. See image.
4. Store the PAT for authenticating with DSPM.

[Image: Creating a programmatic access token for a user in the Snowflake admin panel UI]

To create a role and grant DSPM with permissions to query the Snowflake data for scanning, run the following command:

```
CREATE ROLE dspmdatascanrole;
 
GRANT usage ON WAREHOUSE dspmwarehouse TO ROLE dspmdatascanrole ;
grant MONITOR SECURITY ON ACCOUNT to role dspmdatascanrole;
grant MONITOR USAGE ON ACCOUNT to role dspmdatascanrole;
GRANT DATABASE ROLE SNOWFLAKE.SECURITY_VIEWER TO ROLE dspmdatascanrole;
```

Run the following script to grant necessary privileges to the role:

```
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE z_dspm_grant_db_read()
RETURNS varchar
LANGUAGE SQL
AS
DECLARE
   cur CURSOR FOR SELECT db_name FROM regular_databases;
   db_name STRING;
   dspm_role_name STRING := 'dspmdatascanrole';
   grants NUMBER := 0;
BEGIN
   SHOW DATABASES;
    
   CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE regular_databases AS
   SELECT "name" AS db_name
   FROM TABLE(RESULT_SCAN(LAST_QUERY_ID()))
   WHERE "origin" = '';
   FOR record IN cur DO
       db_name := record.db_name;
       EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'GRANT USAGE ON DATABASE "' || db_name || '" TO ROLE ' ||  dspm_role_name;
        
       EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'GRANT USAGE ON ALL SCHEMAS IN DATABASE "' || db_name || '" TO ROLE ' ||  dspm_role_name;
       EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'GRANT USAGE ON FUTURE SCHEMAS IN DATABASE "' || db_name || '" TO ROLE ' ||  dspm_role_name;
        
       EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN DATABASE "' || db_name || '" TO ROLE ' ||  dspm_role_name;
       EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'GRANT SELECT ON FUTURE TABLES IN DATABASE "' || db_name || '" TO ROLE ' ||  dspm_role_name;
       grants := grants + 5;
   END FOR;
    
   RETURN grants || ' grants executed on non-shared databases.';
END;
```

Run the following `grant` procedure that the script created:

```
CALL z_dspm_grant_db_read();
```

Optional: In case you want this DSPM role to automatically discover and scan the newly added databases, run the following command once. This creates a Snowflake task that runs the `grant` procedure at regular intervals to get access to any newly added databases:

```
CALL z_dspm_grant_db_read();
CREATE OR REPLACE TASK z_dspm_role_grant_task
   schedule = 'USING CRON 0 2 * * * UTC'   -- runs every day at 2am UTC; edit as needed
AS
   CALL z_dspm_grant_db_read();
```

A dedicated warehouse is required so that DSPM has the necessary resources in Snowflake.

Run the following command in Snowflake to create a warehouse:

```
CREATE OR ALTER WAREHOUSE dspmwarehouse;
- By default this will create with size x-small
```

## Adding a Snowflake Account

To add a Snowflake account:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Service Registration**.
2. On the **Service Registration** page, select the **Snowflake** tab, and click **Add Account**. See image. The **Add Snowflake Account** drawer appears.
3. In the **Add Snowflake Account** drawer, update the required fields:
  1. In the **Account Information** section: See image.
    1. **Account Alias** (Optional): Enter a name to identify the Snowflake account in DSPM.
    2. **Account Edition**: Select the edition of the Snowflake account.
    3. **Account Name**: Snowflake account name as configured in the Snowflake.
    4. **Organization Name**: Enter the Snowflake organization name.
    5. **Cloud Provider**: Select the cloud service provider hosting the Snowflake account (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
    6. **Cloud Region**: Search for and select the region where the Snowflake account is located.
    7. **Business Unit**: Assign the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) to the Snowflake account.
    8. **DSPM Integration Alias**: Enter the DSPM alias for the Snowflake account.
  2. In the **Authentication** section, select the **Secret Provider Type**: The authentication option differs depending on the cloud service provider.
    - AWS Secrets Manager
    - Azure Key Vault
    - GCP Secrets Manager
4. Click **Save**.

After registration, verify the connection between DSPM and the Snowflake server. To learn more, see [Testing Connection for Registered Services](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/test-connection-registered-services).

The Snowflake account is added and displayed on the [Snowflake](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-service-registration) page. You can proceed to [configure the scan rule](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-rule-snowflake-databases).

For the **Authentication Type**, select any of the following:

- Key-Pair See image.
  - **Username**: Enter the DSPM username.
  - **Private Key AWS Secret ARN**: Enter the ARN of the HashiCorp Vault instance where the database credentials are stored.
  - **Passphrase AWS Secret ARN** (Optional): Enter the ARN of the HashiCorp Vault instance where the database credentials are passphrased.
- Username/Password See image.
  - **Username**: Enter the DSPM username.
  - **AWS Secret ARN**: Enter the ARN of the secret in which the password is stored. In order for DSPM to read the password and connect to the database, ensure to create and store the secret in the AWS account where the orchestrator account is present.

For the **Authentication Type**, select any of the following:

- Key-Pair See image.
  - **Username**: Enter the DSPM username.
  - **Private Key Azure Key Vault URI**: Enter the URI of the HashiCorp Vault instance where the database credentials are stored.
  - **Passphrase Azure Key Vault URI** (Optional): Enter the URI of the HashiCorp Vault instance where the database credentials are passphrased.
- Username/Password See image.
  - **Username**: Enter the DSPM username.
  - **Azure Key Vault URI**: Enter the URI of the secret storing the password. In order for DSPM to read the password and connect to the database, ensure to create and store the secret in the Key Vault of the worker plane resource group [`integration_id_worker_plane_rg`] of the Azure subscription where the orchestrator account is present.

For the **Authentication Type**, select any of the following:

- Key-Pair See image.
  - **Username**: Enter the DSPM username.
  - **Private Key GCP Secret ID**: Enter the Secret ID path of the HashiCorp Vault instance where the database credentials are stored.
  - **Passphrase GCP Secret ID** (Optional): Enter the Secret ID path of the HashiCorp Vault instance where the database credentials are passphrased.
- Username/Password See image.
  - **Username**: Enter the DSPM username.
  - **GCP Secret ID**: Enter the Secret ID path of the secret storing the password. In order for DSPM to read the password and connect to the database, ensure to create and store the secret in the secret manager of the GCP project where the orchestrator account is present.

[Image: Add Snowflake Account drawer with the necessary account information details filled.]

[Image: The Snowflake page with a list of accounts and annotation around the Add Account button.]

[Image: AWS authentication with Username, and AWS Secret ARN.]

[Image: AWS authentication with Key-Pair.]

[Image: Azure authentication with Username, and Azure Key Vault URI.]

[Image: Azure authentication with Key-Pair.]

[Image: GCP authentication with Username, and GCP Secret ID.]

[Image: GCP authentication with Key-Pair.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/adding-unmanaged-database","lastmod":"2026-05-24T07:06Z","nid":"1517566"} -->
## Adding Unmanaged Databases

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-unmanaged-database
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Service Registration > Unmanaged Databases > Adding Unmanaged Databases
- Last modified: 2026-05-24T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about how to add an unmanaged database server in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can add an [unmanaged database server](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-unmanaged-database) to DSPM. DSPM scans the unmanaged databases for sensitive data and identifies any potential security posture risks.

## Prerequisites

Before adding unmanaged databases to DSPM, ensure the following prerequisites are met:

- 1. [Onboard the account using a custom model](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#SelectNetworkConfiguration) to establish network connectivity between DSPM and the unmanaged database.
- 2. Modify security groups to allow connections from the scanner or orchestrator subnets.
- 3. Create a [custom role with required permissions to configure SQL authentication.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-sql-authentication-unmanaged-databases)
- 4. Provide SQL connection strings and authentication credentials to allow DSPM to access the unmanaged database.
- 5. If the database uses a self-hosted HashiCorp Vault:
  - Ensure the network policies allow inbound connectivity from the DSPM scanner subnets to the HashiCorp Vault and unmanaged databases.
  - Create a DSPM user in the HashiCorp Vault for authentication.
  - Add secrets in the HashiCorp Vault to allow DSPM to fetch the credentials and connect to the unmanaged database to scan sensitive data. To learn more, refer to the [HashiCorp documentation](https://developer.hashicorp.com/vault/docs/commands/secrets).
- 6. Store credentials in the correct secret provider and location.

- **AWS**: Create and store the password or key‑pair in AWS Secrets Manager, and have the ARNs ready for use.
  - **On-premises resources**: Store the secret in the orchestrator account.
  - **Unmanaged database**: Store the secret in the target account.
  1. Open the **AWS Secrets Manager** in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/).
  2. Select **Store a new secret**.
  3. On the **Choose secret type** page: See image.
    1. **Secret type**: Select **Other type of secret**.
    2. **Key/value pairs**: Select the **Plaintext** tab and enter the generated secret.
  4. Click **Next**.
  5. On the **Configure secret** page: See image
    1. **Secret name**: Enter a name for the secret.
    2. **Description** (optional): Enter a description if required.
  6. Click **Next**.
  7. On the **Configure rotation** page, click **Next**.
  8. On the **Review** page, review your secret details, and then click **Store**. See image.
- **Azure**: Create and store the secret in the Azure Key Vault of the worker plane resource group in the subscription where the orchestrator account is present, and have the Key Vault URIs ready for use. To learn more, refer to the [Microsoft documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/secrets/quick-create-portal).
- **GCP**: Create and store the secret in Secret Manager within the GCP project where the orchestrator account is present, and have the Secret ID paths ready for use. To learn more, refer to the [GCP documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/creating-and-accessing-secrets).

[Image: Review secret details window to verify the secret details]

[Image: Configure secret window to configure the name of the secret.]

[Image: AWS Secret Manager window showing options to store new secrets.]

## Adding an Unmanaged Database Server

To add an unmanaged database server:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Service Registration**.
2. On the **Service Registration** page, select the **Unmanaged Database** tab. To add database servers, do one of the following:
  - Add a database server
  - Download the template
  - Upload multiple database servers

After registration, verify the connection between DSPM and the database server. For on-premises unmanaged databases, DSPM runs the test automatically after registration. For cloud unmanaged databases, like Snowflake and Databricks, you must run the test manually. To learn more, see [Testing Connection for Registered Services](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/test-connection-registered-services).

To configure the scan settings, see [Configuring Scan Settings for Azure Unmanaged Databases](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-settings-azure-unmanaged-database), [Configuring Scan Settings for On-Premises Unmanaged Database](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-settings-premise-unmanaged-database), and [Configuring Scan Settings for AWS Unmanaged Databases](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-settings-aws-unmanaged-databases).

1. Click **Download Template**. See image. A ZIP file named `onprem_unmanageddb` is downloaded to your system.
2. Extract the ZIP file. It contains the following files:
  - `cloud_unmanageddb.xlsx` for cloud databases
  - `onprem_unmanageddb.xlsx` for on‑premises databases

[Image: The Unmanaged Databases page with a list of databases and annotation around the Download Template option.]

1. Add the database server details to the template file you downloaded in the previous step.
  - On-premises
  - Cloud
2. Click **Upload Database Servers**. See image.
3. In the **Upload Database Servers** window, upload the template file that contains the details. The uploaded file name must be exactly `onprem_unmanageddb.xlsx` for on‑premises databases or `cloud_unmanageddb.xlsx` for cloud databases, to prevent errors.
4. See image.
5. Click **Upload**.

The unmanaged database servers are added and displayed on the [Unmanaged Databases](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-unmanaged-database) page.

[Image: The Unmanaged Databases page with a list of databases and annotation around Upload Database Servers button..]

[Image: The Upload Database Servers window displays the uploaded template file, with an annotation around the Upload button.]

- **Data Center**: The name of the data center where the database server is located.
- **Database Server Name**: A unique name for the database server.
- **Database Version**: The version of the database server.
- **Connection String**: The connection string required to connect to the database server.
- **UserName**: The username that DSPM uses to connect to the database.
- **Password**: The login password for the username to connect to the unmanaged database.

- **Cloud Type**: The cloud service provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) where your database server is hosted.
- **Cloud Account**: The cloud account in which the database server is stored.
- **Cloud Region**: The region where the database server is located.
- **Virtual Machine ID**: The virtual machine ID or an EC2 instance ID that must be associated with the database server.
- **Database Server Name**: A unique name for the database server.
- **Database Version**: The version of the database server.
- **Connection String**: The connection string required to connect to the database server.
- **UserName**: The username that DSPM uses to connect to the database.
- **Password**: The login password for the username to connect to the unmanaged database.

1. On the **Service Registration** page, select the **Unmanaged Database** tab, and click **Add Database Server**. See image. The **Add Unmanaged Database Server**drawer appears.
2. In the **Add Unmanaged Database Server** drawer, select the database server type: See image.
  - Cloud Database
  - On-Premises Database
3. In the **Database Server** section: See image.
  1. **Database Server Name**: Enter a unique name for the database server.
  2. **Database Engine**: Select the database engine type (**MS SQL**, **PostgreSQL**, **Oracle**, **MySQL**, or **MongoDB**).
  3. **Database Version**: Select the version of the database server.
  4. **Type of Connection String** (for Oracle Only): Select any of the following connection strings:
    - **Container Database**: A database that contains multiple, independent databases called Pluggable Databases (PDBs).
    - **Pluggable Database**: A portable collection of schemas, schema objects, and non-schema objects.
    - **Database Instance**: This is a set of memory structures and background processes to manage database files.
  5. **Connection String**: Enter the connection string required to connect to the database server.
4. In the **Authentication** section: The authentication type differs depending on the deployment type and database engine. For cloud deployments, authentication is based on the cloud type.; For on-premises deployments, authentication is based on the associated cloud network. **Secret Provider Type**: Select the secret provider used for authentication. Azure Key Vault or AWS Secrets Manager; Self Hosted HashiCorp Vault; Zscaler DSPM
5. **Database Authentication**: This is applicable when HashiCorp Vault is selected as the **Secret Provider Type**. See image.
  1. **Authentication Type**: Select the authentication type to authenticate to the unmanaged database.
  2. **Username**: Enter the username that DSPM uses to connect to the unmanaged database. This should match the username stored in the HashiCorp Vault secret.
  3. **HashiCorp Vault Secret Path**: Enter the HashiCorp Vault path where the secret is stored. For example, `hashicorp/vault/zscaler/password`.
  4. **HashiCorp Vault Secret Key**: Enter the HashiCorp key that stores the database login password.
6. Click **Save**.

The unmanaged database server is added and displayed on the [Unmanaged Databases](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-unmanaged-database) page.

1. **Authentication Type**(for MongoDB database engine only): Select **SCRAM Authentication** or **X.509 Authentication**.
2. **Username**: Enter the username that DSPM uses to connect to the unmanaged database.
3. **Password**: Enter the login password for the username to connect to the unmanaged database.
4. **Certificate Authority (.pem)**(Optional for MongoDB database engine only): Drag and drop or click to browse to provide the PEM Certificate Authority (CA) certificate file.
5. **Client Certificate (.pem)**(Optional for MongoDB database engine only): Drag and drop or click to browse to provide the PEM certificate file.
6. **Client Key Password**(Optional for MongoDB database engine only): Enter the passphrase to decrypt the certificate if the uploaded certificate (PEM) file is encrypted. This private key must correspond to the client certificate provided in the preceding details.

See image.

[Image: Adding Unmanaged Database Server - Authentication section with the details filled.]

1. **Endpoint**: Enter the URL of the HashiCorp Vault.
2. **Username**: Enter the login username of the HashiCorp Vault.
3. **Key Vault URI** or **AWS Secrets Manager ARN**: Enter the secret URI or ARN where HashiCorp vault login password is saved. The label of this field changes based on the selected cloud provider:
  - For AWS, it appears as **Secrets Manager ARN**.
  - For Azure, it appears as **Key Vault URI**.

See image.

- **Authentication Type**: Select the authentication type (**SQL Authentication**, **Microsoft Entra Service Principal**, **Microsoft Entra Authentication with user-managed identity**, **SCRAM Authentication**, or **X.509 Authentication**).
  - SQL Authentication (For Azure, AWS, and On-Premises)
  - Microsoft Entra Service Principal (for Azure only)
  - Microsoft Entra Authentication with User Managed Identity (for Azure only)
  - SCRAM Authentication, or X.509 Authentication (for MongoDB database engine only)

1. **Associate Database Server with Virtual Machine**: Enable the toggle to associate the database server with a virtual machine.
2. **Cloud Type**: Select the cloud service provider (AWS, Azure, or GCP) where your database server is hosted.
3. **Account**: Select the cloud account in which the database server is stored.
4. **Cloud Region**: Select the region where the database server is located.
5. **Virtual Machine**: Select the virtual machine or an EC2 instance that must be associated with the database server. The **Virtual Machine** option is only available when the **Associate Database Server with Virtual Machine** toggle is enabled.

See image.

In the **Data Center Information** section:

1. **Data Center**: Select the name of the data center where the database server is located.
2. **Location**: This is automatically populated based on the selected data center. See image. If the data center has on-premises scanners, then the **On-Premise Scanner** section is automatically populated with the available integrations. If not, integrate an on-premises scanner with the data center. To learn more, see [Adding or Deleting a Scanner Integration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-or-deleting-scanner-integration). See image.

1. **Username** (for SCRAM Authentication only): Enter the MongoDB username that DSPM uses to connect to the database.
2. **Password Secret (ARN**or **URI)** (for SCRAM Authentication only): Enter the unique identifier for the secret that contains the password for the specified username.
  - For AWS: **Secrets Manager ARN**
  - For Azure: **Key Vault URI**
3. **Certificate Authority (ARN**or **URI)**(Optional): Enter the ARN or URI of the secret containing the Certificate Authority (CA) certificate.
4. **Client Certificate (ARN**or **URI)**(Optional for SCRAM Authentication): Enter the ARN or URI of the secret containing the public certificate file.
5. **Client Key (ARN**or **URI)**(Optional): Enter the ARN or URI of the secret containing the passphrase to decrypt the certificate if the uploaded certificate (PEM) file is encrypted. This private key must correspond to the client certificate provided in the preceding steps.

See image.

1. **Username**: Enter the username for SQL authentication.
2. **Key Vault URI**: Enter the Uniform Resource Indicator (URI), a unique identifier of the Key Vault instance. In order for DSPM to read the password and connect to the database, ensure you do the following:
  | Database Type | Secret Storage Details |

When using SQL Authentication, [create a custom server reader role with the necessary permissions](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-sql-authentication-unmanaged-databases) to scan the database.

1. **Application ID**: Enter the application ID for Microsoft Entra authentication.
2. **AWS Secret Manager ARN** (for AWS): Enter the ARN of the AWS Secret Manager. This ARN must be available in the account where the unmanaged database is located.
3. **Key Vault URI**(for Azure): Enter the Uniform Resource Indicator (URI) of the Key Vault instance. This URI must be available in the same account where the unmanaged database is present, and the Key Vault should follow the `Azure role-based access control` permission model.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/alert-status","lastmod":"2026-04-15T00:38Z","nid":"1487771"} -->
## Alert Status

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/alert-status
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Alerts > Alert Details > Alert Status
- Last modified: 2026-04-15T00:38Z
- Summary: Information about DSPM alert statuses in the Zscaler Admin Console.

When a policy violation is detected in your cloud resources, DSPM generates alerts and notifies recipients to take action. These generated alerts are displayed on the [Alerts page](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alerts). Alerts that are initially generated are in Open status. When these alerts are evaluated and addressed, the status transitions to Resolved, Closed, or Snoozed.

DSPM alerts can have the following status:

| Alert Status | Description | Example Scenarios | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | The new alerts generated for a policy violation or resolved alerts for which policy violation is detected again. | A [policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-posture-policies) violation is detected.; The policy violation is detected again within 180 days of resolving the alert. | An open alert moves to the resolved, closed, or snoozed state based on the latest policy findings, [manual actions](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-alerts) (resolve, snooze, unsnooze, or reset), or alert filter ([ignore alert filter](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-ignore-alert-filters)).; When a [data store](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/supported-data-stores) is removed from the [scan settings](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings), the alerts remain open based on the posture assessment of the data store.; An automatically resolved alert is reopened if the violation is detected within 180 days of resolving the alert. The Alert Status Reason in an individual alert's page describes the reason for why the alert is reopened.; DSPM generates a new alert if the policy violation is detected again after 180 days. |
| Closed | The alerts that are no longer valid. | The [cloud account](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloud-accounts) is offboarded.; The cloud account is deleted from the CSP.; The policy is edited, disabled, or deleted.; The data store is deleted.; The data store that was removed earlier is not added back to the scan settings. | A closed alert is the final state of an alert (i.e., it does not move to any other state).; The [alert graph](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-alert-graph) for a closed alert is frozen and the nodes are unclickable.; The [Sensitive Data](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-sensitive-data-details) tab in an individual alert's page is hidden.; The closed alert is deleted from the Zscaler Admin Console after 180 days. |
| Resolved | The policy violation detected in the data store is fixed. | The alert is manually resolved in the Zscaler Admin Console.; The policy violation is manually [remediated](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-remediation-details).; The policy violation is resolved in the CSP. | An automatically resolved alert moves to the open state if the issue is detected within 180 days of resolving the alert. DSPM generates a new alert if the policy violation is detected again after 180 days.; A manually resolved alert remains in the resolved state until you reset it. When you reset the alert, the alert status is updated based on the latest policy findings.; A resolved alert moves to the closed state if the data store, policy, or cloud account is deleted.; The alert graph for a resolved alert is frozen, and the nodes are unclickable.; The [Sensitive Data](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-sensitive-data-details) tab in an individual alert's page is hidden. |
| Snoozed | Alerts of low priority that are paused for a specific duration. | The alert is manually snoozed to pause notification for a specified duration. | A snoozed alert remains snoozed even if the policy violation is resolved in the CSP.; If you unsnooze an alert or if the snooze period expires, the alert status changes to open or resolved based on the latest policy findings.; If the data store or policy is deleted when the alert is snoozed, the alert moves to the closed state irrespective of the snooze period.; If the policy violation is resolved in the CSP, the alert graph freezes, and the nodes become unclickable. |
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/changing-aws-cloudtrail-details","lastmod":"2026-04-24T22:52Z","nid":"1478051"} -->
## Changing AWS CloudTrail Details

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/changing-aws-cloudtrail-details
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > CloudTrail > Changing AWS CloudTrail Details
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:52Z
- Summary: Information about how to change CloudTrail details in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can change the [CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-aws-cloudtrail) for an organization or a single account within the organization as required.

## Prerequisites

- You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or any role with Edit Cloud Accounts permission.
- To configure a cross-account CloudTrail that stores logs in an S3 bucket located in a different account than the onboarded account (member account), enable the following settings:
  - CloudTrail Permissions for Member Accounts
  - Cross-Account Log Decryption
  - KMS Key ID

## Changing AWS CloudTrail for an Organization

The organization CloudTrail shares the CloudTrail events of the management and member accounts of the organization to the same CloudTrail S3 bucket. When you reset the organization AWS CloudTrail details, the existing CloudTrail is disabled and all the onboarded accounts move to the [Needs Attention](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarding-status)state until the new CloudTrail is validated successfully.

To change AWS CloudTrail for an organization:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the organization account for which you want to change the CloudTrail details. See image.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Manage CloudTrail** from the drop-down menu. See image.
4. In the **Organization CloudTrail** window:
  1. Click **Reset** to edit the existing CloudTrail details and add new details. See image.
  2. **CloudTrail Type**: If it is an [organization CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-aws-cloudtrail), select the **OrgCloudTrail** checkbox.
  3. **CloudTrail Bucket Name**: Enter the S3 bucket name that is associated with the CloudTrail.
  4. **Prefix (Optional)**: Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail S3 bucket path, if any. See image.
  5. **Bucket Account ID**: Enter the AWS account ID where the CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.
  6. Click **Apply**. See image. A message appears indicating that the CloudTrail details is saved successfully.
  7. Under **Download and Deploy Template,**select one of the following template types:
    - CloudFormation
    - Terraform
  8. Click **Done**.
5. In the **Overview** tab, under the **CloudTrail** section, click **Validate**. See image. After the CloudTrail is validated successfully, the CloudTrail status shows as **Enabled**. See image. If there is any issue found while validating the template, the status of the CloudTrail shows **Failed**. Download the template and run it again, and then validate the CloudTrail. See image.

## Changing AWS CloudTrail for Single or Multiple Accounts

When you update the account CloudTrail, the existing CloudTrail is disabled only for that account, without affecting the other accounts in the organization. The account moves to the [Needs Attention](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarding-status) state until the new CloudTrail is validated successfully.

To change AWS CloudTrail for single or multiple accounts:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the AWS account and then select the **Accounts** tab. See image.
3. Choose one of the following options:
  - To change CloudTrail for a single account: Click the **Actions** icon for the account you want to change the CloudTrail details, then select **Update CloudTrail**. See image.
  - To change CloudTrail for multiple accounts:
    1. Select the checkboxes for the required accounts.
    2. From the **Actions**drop-down menu, select **Update CloudTrail**. See image.
4. In the **Update Account CloudTrail** window: DSPM validates the template deployment by checking the new CloudTrail details provided. If there is any error while validating the template, download and rerun the template. You can see the CloudTrail details of the account in the corresponding account drawer. See image.
  1. Click **Reset** to edit the existing CloudTrail details and add new details. See image.
  2. **CloudTrail Bucket Name**: Enter the S3 bucket name that is associated with CloudTrail.
  3. **Prefix (Optional)**: Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail S3 bucket path, if any.
  4. **Bucket Account ID**: Enter the AWS account ID where the CloudTrail S3 bucket is present. See image.
  5. Click **Apply**. A message appears indicating that the CloudTrail details is saved successfully.
  6. Under **Download and Deploy Template,**select one of the following template types:
    - CloudFormation
    - Terraform
  7. Click **Done**.

To update the CloudTrail details using the CloudFormation template:

- i. Download the CloudFormation template.
- ii. Update the stack.

In the **Organization CloudTrail** window, click **Organization CloudTrail** to download the template as a YAML file to your local system.

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) using the root account credentials and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Stacks**.
3. Identify the stack created while [onboarding an organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization) and click the stack name. See image.
4. Click **Update**. See image.
5. On the **Update stack** page: See image.
  - **Prepare template**: Select **Replace current template**.
  - **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file** and click **Choose file**. Browse your folder and select the downloaded YAML file, then click **Open**.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **Specify stack details** page, click **Next**.
8. On the **Configure stack options** page, click **Next**.
9. On the **Review stack** page, review the stack details and then select the **I acknowledge** checkbox to acknowledge AWS CloudFormation's creation of IAM resources with custom names. See image.
10. Click **Submit**. On the **Events** tab, you can view the status of the stack execution. See image.

To update the CloudTrail details using the Terraform template:

- i. Download the Terraform template.
- ii. Copy the access keys of the root account.
- iii. Run the Terraform template.

In the **Organization CloudTrail** window, click **Organization CloudTrail** to download the template as a Terraform file to your local system.

Copy the **Access keys** of the root account. The access keys provide DSPM with administrator access to the root account from the AWS CLI.

To copy the access keys:

1. Sign in to the AWS access portal and select the root account.
2. Click **Access keys**. See image.
3. Select the required tab (macOS/Linux, Windows, PowerShell) based on your operating system.
4. Under **Option 1: Set AWS environment variables**, click **Copy**. See image.

1. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
2. Switch to the directory that contains the downloaded template .tf folder.
3. Paste the access keys you copied earlier and press `Enter`.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: ``terraform init``See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: ``terraform plan``
  3. To run the Terraform script: ``terraform apply``See image. Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes`and press `Enter`. See image.

To update the CloudTrail details using the CloudFormation template:

- i. Download the CloudFormation template.
- ii. Create a stack.

In the **Update Account CloudTrail** window, click**CloudTrail** to download the template as a YAML file to your local system.

See image.

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) for the account you want to change the CloudTrail, and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Stacks**.
3. Click **Create stack**. See image.
4. On the **Create stack** page:
  1. **Prepare template**: Select **Choose an existing template**.
  2. **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file**to upload the template you downloaded from the Zscaler Admin Console.
  3. **Upload a template file**: Click **Choose file**, browse and select template, then click **Open**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Specify stack details**page, under **Stack name**, enter a unique stack name. See image.
7. Click **Next**.
8. On the **Configure stack options** page, click **Next**.
9. On the **Review and create** page, under **Capabilities**, select the **I acknowledge** checkbox to acknowledge AWS CloudFormation's creation of IAM resources with custom names. See image.
10. Click **Submit**.

To update the CloudTrail details using the Terraform template:

- i. Download the Terraform template.
- ii. Copy the access keys of the account for which you want to change the CloudTrail details.
- iii. Run the Terraform template.

In the **Update Account CloudTrail** window, select **Terraform** and click**CloudTrail** to download the template as a Terraform file to your local system.

See image.

The access keys provide DSPM with administrator access to the account from the AWS CLI.

To copy the access keys:

1. Sign in to the AWS access portal and select the account for which you want to change the CloudTrail details.
2. Click **Access keys**. See image.
3. Select the required tab (macOS/Linux, Windows, PowerShell) based on your operating system.
4. Under **Option 1: Set AWS environment variables**, click **Copy**. See image.

1. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
2. Switch to the directory that contains the downloaded template .tf folder.
3. Paste the access keys you copied earlier and press `Enter`.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: ``terraform init``See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: ``terraform plan``
  3. To run the Terraform script: ``terraform apply``See image. Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes`and press `Enter`. See image.

1. Sign in to the [AWS account](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) where the S3 bucket that stores CloudTrail logs is available, and go to **CloudTrail**.
2. Under **Trails**, select the required CloudTrail.
3. Under **General details**, click the **Trail log location**. See image.
4. Select the S3 bucket, and then select the **Permissions**tab. See image.
5. Under **Bucket policy**, click **Edit**and add the following permissions to write CloudTrail logs of the member accounts in the S3 bucket: `{ "Sid": "AllowCloudTrailWriteLogsFor*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" }, "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::cross-bucketpolicy/AWSLogs/*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*/*", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "AWS:SourceArn": "arn:aws:cloudtrail:us-west-2:*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*:trail/cross-trail", "s3:x-amz-acl": "bucket-owner-full-control" } }``{ "Sid": "AllowBucketAccessForMembers", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": [ "arn iam::*<*CloudTrail account ID*>*: root" ] } }`
6. Click **Save changes**. See image.

2. Copy the S3 bucket name of the CloudTrail.
3. Sign in to the member account, and go to **CloudTrail**.
4. Click **Create trail**.
5. On the **Choose trail attributes** page: See image.

  3. **Trail log bucket name**: Paste the CloudTrail bucket name.
  4. **AWS KMS alias**: Enter the KMS alias.
  5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Choose log events** page: See image.

7. On the **Review and create** page, click **Create trail**.
8. On the **Trails**page, click the newly created trail.
9. Under **General**details, click **AWS KMS key** to update the policy and provide access to the S3 bucket where the CloudTrail is present.
10. On the **Key policy** tab, click **Edit**to add the following policies: See image. `"Sid": "Enable IAM User Permissions", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": [ "arn:aws:iam::*<*CloudTrail Account ID*>*:root", "arn:aws:iam::*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*:role/DSPM-Role-org-1stjuly", "arn:aws:sts::*<*CloudTrail Account ID*>*:assumed-role/AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_2d4e2733faaf72bb/*<userID>*" ] },``{ "Sid": "Enable cross account log decryption", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": [ "arn:aws:iam::*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*:role/DSPM-Role-org-1stjuly-get-data-events", "arn:aws:iam::*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*:role/DSPM-Role-org-1stjuly" ] }, "Action": [ "kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncryptFrom" ], "Resource": "*", "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "kms:CallerAccount": "*<*S3 bucket account ID*>*" }, "StringLike": { "kms:EncryptionContext:aws:cloudtrail:arn": "arn:aws:cloudtrail:*:*<*CloudTrail Account ID*>*:trail/*" }`See image.

1. Sign in to the [AWS account](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) where the S3 bucket that stores CloudTrail logs is available, and go to **Roles**.
2. Select the [resource discovery](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/iam-roles-and-permissions-aws) role that is created by DSPM.
3. Under **Permissions**, expand **DSPM-CLOUDTRAIL-KMS-POLICY**and click **Edit**.
4. In the **Policy editor**, add the S3 bucket account ID where the KMS key is present. See image. `{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Action": [ "kms:Decrypt", ], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:kms:*:<CloudTrail account ID>:key*", "arn:aws:kms:*:<S3 bucket account ID>:key*", "Effect": "Allow", "Sid": "DSPMCLOUDTRAILKMSPOLICY" } ] }`You can also add a specific KMS key: Go to **KMS**> **Customer-managed keys** >**Key ID**.; Copy the **Key ID** and paste it in the Policy editor. `"arn:aws:kms:*:<S3 bucket account ID>:key <kms key ID>",`
5. Click **Save**.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/changing-aws-orchestrator-account","lastmod":"2026-04-24T22:56Z","nid":"1478011"} -->
## Changing an AWS Orchestrator Account

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/changing-aws-orchestrator-account
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Changing an AWS Orchestrator Account
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:56Z
- Summary: Information on how to change an orchestrator account to a different one for AWS in the Zscaler Admin Console.

DSPM regularly scans the data stores of the target accounts by leveraging the [orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-orchestrator) deployed in the AWS orchestrator account while onboarding.

After [onboarding an organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization), you can change the orchestrator account if the existing orchestrator account is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect account was selected while onboarding. When you change the orchestrator account, you must run the orchestrator template in the new account. DSPM validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

Until the new orchestrator account is successfully validated, the following changes occur:

- The existing orchestrator is disabled.
- The DSPM connection status moves to the Waiting for Connection state and Configuration status moves to the Pending state.
- The data scans are stopped.
- The target accounts move to the Needs Attention state.

## Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an [administrator](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) role or a custom role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

## Changing an Orchestrator Account

To change the orchestrator account:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the organization for which you want to change the orchestrator account.
3. Click **Manage** and then select **Configure New Orchestrator**. See image.
4. In the **Configure New Orchestrator** window, read the caution and then select the **I understand** checkbox. See image.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. In the **Configure an Orchestrator Account** page, select the account and primary region where you want to deploy the orchestrator template, and then click **Next**. See image. The existing orchestrator account checkbox is disabled. See image.
7. In the **Provide Permissions** page, download and run the templates. Before running the template on the new orchestrator account, purge the template that was previously deployed on the existing orchestrator account. You can do this by deleting the corresponding stackset or running the `terraform destroy` command based on the template type. See image.
  1. [Run the orchestrator template.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization#runorchtemplate)
  2. [Run the monitoring template.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization#runmonitoringscopetemplate)
8. Click **Done**.

DSPM validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles created and permissions granted.

If there is any issue while deploying the template, an error is displayed. Rerun the templates in the orchestrator account and target accounts.

After the template deployment is validated successfully, the target accounts move to the Successfully Configured state, and DSPM begins the [data scan](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings). The orchestrator status (DSPM Connection and Configuration Status) moves to the Successful state.

See image.

You can view the orchestrator details on the [Overview](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarded-account-details) tab.

[Image: Configure a New Orchestrator page]

[Image: Disabled existing orchestrator checkbox]

[Image: View the orchestrator status]

## Changing a Business Unit

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/changing-business-unit
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Cloud Account Management > Changing a Business Unit
- Last modified: 2026-04-29T21:31Z
- Summary: Information about how to change the business units for the cloud accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can change the business units for each [organization unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization) (OU), [management group](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant), single account, or multiple accounts.

When a business unit is assigned to an OU or a management group, all the accounts within that OU or management group are assigned to the same business unit. For example, if an OU has 5 accounts and BU1 is assigned to the OU, all 5 accounts within that OU are assigned to BU1.

Changing the business unit overrides the currently assigned business unit.

## Prerequisite

You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or any role with the Business Unit Mapping permission.

## Changing a Business Unit for an OU or Management Group

To change a business unit for an OU or management group:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account (AWS organization, Microsoft Entra tenant or GCP organization).
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Business Units Mapping** from the drop-down menu. See image.
4. On the **Business Units Mapping** page, assign a business unit to the OU. All the accounts in the OU are mapped to the selected business unit. See image.
5. Click **Done**. A message appears indicating that the business unit was changed successfully.

## Changing a Business Unit for Single or Multiple Accounts

To change a business unit for single or multiple accounts:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account:
  - AWS
  - Azure
  - GCP
3. In the **Change Business Unit for Selected** window, select the business unit from the drop-down menu. See image.
4. Click **Apply**. A message appears indicating that the business unit was changed successfully.

1. Select the organization and then select the **Accounts** tab. See image.
2. Choose any of the following options:
  - To change a business unit for a single account: Click the **Actions** icon for the account you want to change the business unit, then select **Change Business Unit**. See image.
  - To change a business unit for multiple accounts:
    1. Select the checkboxes for the required accounts. The **Actions** menu appears on the page. See image.
    2. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Change Business Unit**. See image.

1. Select the tenant and then select the **Subscriptions** tab. See image.
2. Choose any of the following options:
  - To change a business unit for a single subscription: Click the **Actions** icon for the subscription you want to change the business unit, then select **Change Business Unit**. See image.
  - To change a business unit for multiple subscriptions:
    1. Select the checkboxes for the required subscriptions. The **Actions** menu appears on the page. See image.
    2. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Change Business Unit**. See image.

1. Select the organization and then select the **Projects** tab. See image.
2. Choose any of the following options:
  - To change a business unit for a single project: Click the **Actions** icon for the project you want to change the business unit, then select **Change Business Unit**. See image.
  - To change a business unit for multiple projects:
    1. Select the checkboxes for the required projects. The **Actions** menu appears on the page. See image.
    2. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Change Business Unit**. See image.

## Changing a GCP Orchestrator Account

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/changing-gcp-orchestrator-account
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > GCP Cloud Accounts > Changing a GCP Orchestrator Account
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:34Z
- Summary: Information on how to change an orchestrator account to a different one for GCP in the Zscaler Admin Console.

DSPM regularly scans the data stores of the target projects by leveraging the [orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-orchestrator) deployed in the GCP orchestrator project while onboarding.

After [onboarding an organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-gcp-organization), you can change the orchestrator project if the existing orchestrator project is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect project was selected while onboarding. When you change the orchestrator project, you must run the orchestrator template in the new project. DSPM validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

Until the new orchestrator project is successfully validated, the following changes occur:

- The existing orchestrator is disabled.
- The DSPM connection status moves to the Waiting for Connection state and Configuration status moves to the Pending state.
- The data scans are stopped.
- The target projects move to the Needs Attention state.

## Prerequisites

Be assigned either an [administrator](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions)role or a custom role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

## Changing Orchestrator Subscription

To change the orchestrator project:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the organization to which you want to change the orchestrator subscription.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Configure New Orchestrator** from the drop-down menu. See image.
4. In the **New Orchestrator** window, read the caution and then select the **I understand** checkbox. See image.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. In the **Configure an Orchestrator project**page:
  - Select an orchestrator project on which you want to deploy the DSPM's orchestrator template.
  - **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator project.
  - **Log Bucket Name**: Enter a unique name for the log bucket. This log bucket stores the activity logs of the target projects. The log bucket is created while deploying the onboarding template. The name must be unique, otherwise DSPM shows an error message.
7. Click **Next**.
8. In the **Grant Permissions** section, download the GCP onboarding template, which includes policies and permissions to create custom roles in the GCP organization, and deploy it on your cloud account. This template provides DSPM with the permissions to access the organization. Before running the template on the new orchestrator subscription, purge the template that was previously deployed on the existing orchestrator by running the `terraform destroy` command.
  - a. In the Zscaler Admin Console
  - b. On the Local System
9. Click **Done**. DSPM validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles that are created and permissions granted. An error message appears if there is any issue while deploying the template. Rerun the template in the root account. After the template is successfully deployed, the DSPM begins the [data scan](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings) for the onboarded projects, and you are directed to the [Overview page](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarding-status) to view the status of the onboarded project and orchestrator details.

Click **GCP Onboarding** to download the template as a ZIP file.

See image.

[Image: Download GCP Onboarding Template]

Update and run the template in the gcloud using the CLI app:

1. Extract the downloaded ZIP file to a local directory on your system.
2. Locate the `backend.tf` file within the extracted folder and open it in a text editor. See image.
3. Update the file by adding the name of the storage bucket and a preferred prefix where you would like to store the Terraform state files, and then, save and close the `backend.tf` file. See image.
4. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app on your local system.
5. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
6. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the working directory and apply the Terraform configuration: `terraform init`See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want DSPM to monitor and scan data in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`DSPM creates resources required for data scanning only in these specified regions. See image.
  3. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`See image. For **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`. See image.

[Image: Initialise the Terraform]

[Image: Orchestrator Terraform Template Plan]

[Image: Terraform apply]

[Image: Confirm Terraform Apply]

[Image: Confirm New Orchestrator Configuration]

## Changing an Azure Orchestrator Subscription

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/changing-orchestrator-subscription
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Changing an Azure Orchestrator Subscription
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:46Z
- Summary: Information on how to change an orchestrator subscription to a different one for Azure in the Zscaler Admin Console.

DSPM uses the [orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/understanding-orchestrator) that is deployed on the Azure subscription to scan the data stores.

You can change the orchestrator subscription if the existing orchestrator subscription is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect subscription was selected while onboarding. When you change the orchestrator subscription, you must run the orchestrator template in the new subscription. DSPM validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

Until the new orchestrator subscription is successfully validated, the following changes occur:

- The existing orchestrator is disabled.
- The DSPM connection status moves to the Waiting for Connection state and Configuration status moves to the Pending state.
- The data scans are stopped.
- The target subscriptions move to the Needs Attention state.

## Prerequisites

Make sure the following prerequisites are met:

- Be assigned either an [administrator](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) role or any role with the Configure New Orchestrator permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.
- Before redeploying the orchestrator template, you must add your system's IP address to the [Azure storage account](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkId=845586) and [Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-in/azure/key-vault/general/how-to-azure-key-vault-network-security)'s IP networks. This is required when multiple users need to apply Terraform from different IP addresses.

## Changing Orchestrator Subscription

To change the orchestrator subscription:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the tenant for which you want to change the orchestrator subscription.
3. Click **Manage** and then select **Configure New Orchestrator**. See image.
4. In the **Configure New Orchestrator** window, read the caution and then select the **I understand** checkbox. See image.
5. Click **Continue**.
6. In the **Configure an Orchestrator subscription** page: See image.
  - Select a subscription on which you want to deploy the DSPM's orchestrator template.
  - **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator.
  - **Storage Account Name**: Enter a unique name for the storage account. This storage account is used to store the activity logs of the target subscriptions. It is created while running the onboarding template. The storage account name cannot exceed 16 characters.
  - Select the **Deploy private endpoint for secure communication** checkbox to establish a private connection between DSPM and Azure resources. This restricts communication over public IP addresses.
7. Click **Next**.
8. On the **Provide Permissions** page, download the template to run it in the Microsoft Entra tenant. Before running the template on the new orchestrator subscription, purge the previously deployed template by running the `terraform destroy` command.; If the resource group is manually deleted:Import the following resources:`terraform import "module.control_plane[\"region\"].module.encryption_key.azurerm_key_vault_key.cmk_key""resourceID"`; `terraform import "module.worker_plane[\"region\"].module.encryption_key.azurerm_key_vault_key.cmk_key""resourceID"`; Purge the secret key vault:Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Key vaults**.; Click **Manage deleted vaults**.; On the **Manage deleted key vaults** page:**Subscription**: Select the existing orchestrator subscription.; Select the secrets key vault check box and click **Purge**.
  - a. Download the orchestrator template.
  - b. Update and run the Terraform files.
9. Click **Done**.

DSPM validates the template deployment every hour by checking the roles that are created and permissions granted.

An error message appears if there is any issue while deploying the template. Rerun the template in the root account.

After the template is successfully deployed, the onboarded subscriptions move to the Successfully Configured state and DSPM begins the [data scan](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings). The DSPM Connection and Configuration Status for the orchestrator are displayed as successful.

See image.

You can view the orchestrator details on the [Overview](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarding-status) tab.

Click **Azure Onboarding**to download the template as a ZIP file. Extract the file to your local system and create a new folder to store the extracted files. The ZIP file includes multiple Terraform files that contain policies and permissions required for DSPM to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant.

See image.

1. Update the following downloaded files:
  - **backend.tf**: Enter the name of the storage containers where you want to store the Terraform state files. See image.
  - **terraform.tfvars**: Change the random_seed value. Remember this seed value and use the same value when you deploy [new templates](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-roles-and-templates).
2. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
3. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform files.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To connect to your Microsoft Entra tenant: `az login --tenant <tenant ID>`See image. You are directed to a web browser to authorize the Microsoft Entra tenant. Select your account to confirm the authorization. See image. The command output returns the subscriptions available within your Microsoft Entra tenant.
  2. To set the subscription where you want to run the Terraform template: `az account set --subscription <subscription ID>`
  3. (Optional) To verify if the subscription is accurately set: `az account show`
  4. To initialize the working directory and apply Terraform configuration: `terraform init`See image.
  5. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`
  6. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`. See image.

[Image: Configure the working directory]

[Image: Connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant]

[Image: Update the backend file]

[Image: Apply the configuration]

[Image: Select your Azure account]
