<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-application-details-and-client-secret","lastmod":"2026-04-24T22:46Z","nid":"1479331"} -->
## Managing Application Details and Client Secret

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-application-details-and-client-secret
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Managing Application Details and Client Secret
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:46Z
- Summary: How to update application details and client secret for Microsoft Azure.

While [onboarding a Microsoft Entra tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant), a service principal or application is created within the Microsoft Entra tenant. The service principal defines the policies and permissions required for DSPM to access specific resources within the onboarded Microsoft Entra tenant. The service principal is identified by a unique identifier called the application or the client ID, along with a client secret used as a password.

You can update the application details and client secret of the service principal as required.

## Updating Application Details

If the service principal is accidentally deleted, DSPM's access to the onboarded tenant is impacted, and all the onboarded subscriptions within the tenant move to the [Needs Attention](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarding-status) state. To restore access, you must update the application details.

### Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or any role with Change Application Details permissions.

### Updating Application Details

To update the application details:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the tenant for which you want to update the application details.
3. Select the **Roles and Templates** tab.
4. Download and run the **Tree Discovery** template: See image.
  - a. In the Zscaler Admin Console
  - b. On the Local System
  - c. In the Microsoft Entra Tenant
5. Click **Manage** and then select **Change Application Details.** See image.
6. In the **Change Application Details** window, enter the client ID and client secret generated in the CLI app:
  - **Application ID**: Enter the client ID.
  - **Client Secret**: Enter the client secret.
7. Click **Validate**. See image. DSPM validates the template deployment by verifying the application ID, client secret, and the custom roles created. If the validation is successful, a message appears indicating that the connection is established.
8. Click **Done**.
9. On the **Roles and Templates** tab, download and run the **Azure Onboarding**template: See image. After the template is successfully deployed, DSPM's access to the Microsoft Entra tenant is restored, and the onboarded subscriptions move to the Successfully Configured state.
  - a. In the Zscaler Admin Console
  - b. On the Local System

## Updating the Client Secret

The client secret ID in Microsoft Azure is a confidential string that is used as a password for the service principal or application. It comes with an expiration date and must be renewed for the service principal to remain functional. You can update the client secret ID that you provided while [onboarding a tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant).

### Prerequisites

- You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or any role with Change Application Details permissions in the Zscaler Admin Console.
- Ensure that you have added a new client secret for the service principal in the Microsoft Entra tenant.

### Updating the Client Secret

To update the client secret ID:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the tenant for which you want to update the client secret.
3. Click **Manage** and then select **Change Application Details.** See image.
4. In the **Change Application Details** window, for **Client Secret**, paste the string copied from the Microsoft Entra tenant. See image.
5. Click **Validate**. DSPM validates the updated client secret by verifying it against the service principal and application ID. If the validation is successful, a message appears indicating that the connection is established. If the client secret is invalid, or it does not match the service principal, an error is displayed. See image.
6. Click **Done**. The client secret is updated for the service principal.

To add a new client secret:

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Microsoft Entra ID**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **App registrations**. See image.
3. Select the **Owned applications** tab.
4. Search for and select the [service principal](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant) you created while onboarding.
5. In the left-side navigation, select **Certificates & secrets**. See image.
6. On the **Client secrets** tab, click **New client secret**. See image.
7. In the **Add a client secret** page: See image.
  - **Description**: Enter a description for the client secret.
  - **Expires**: Select the expiry date from the drop-down menu.
8. Click **Add**.
9. In the **Client secrets** table, under **Value**, click the copy icon to copy the string to the clipboard. See image.

Click **Tree Discovery** to download the template as a ZIP file. Extract the file to your local system and create a new folder to store the extracted files. The ZIP file contains two Terraform files (`backend.tf` and `azure_tf_basic.tf`).

See image.

Run the template in the Microsoft Entra tenant using the CLI app:

1. Update the downloaded `backend.tf` file with the storage container names where you want to store the Terraform state files. See image.
  - **resource_group_name**: Enter the resource group name.
  - **storage_account_name**: Enter the storage account name.
  - **container_name**: Enter the container name.
2. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
3. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To connect to your Microsoft Entra tenant: `az login --tenant <tenant ID>`See image. You are directed to a web browser to authorize the Microsoft Entra tenant. Select your account to confirm the authorization. See image. The command output returns the subscriptions available within your Microsoft Entra tenant.
  2. To set the subscription where you want to run the Terraform template: `az account set --subscription <subscription ID>`
  3. (Optional) To verify if the subscription is accurately set: `az account show`
  4. To initialize the working directory and apply Terraform configuration: `terraform init`See image.
  5. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`For **Enter a value**: Enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3"]`
  6. To run the script: `terraform apply`For **Enter a value**: Enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3"]`Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`. See image. The command output returns the client ID and client secret that is required to connect DSPM with the Microsoft Entra tenant. See image.

After the template is successfully deployed, a service principal or application is created in the Microsoft Entra tenant. You need to grant API permissions to the service principal to access resources within the Microsoft Entra tenant.

To grant API permissions:

1. Sign in to the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/) and go to **Microsoft Entra ID**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **App registrations**. See image.
3. Select the **Owned applications** tab. See image.
4. In the table, search for and select the service principal.
5. In the left-side navigation, select **API permissions**. See image.
6. Click **Grant admin consent for <tenant name>.** See image.
7. In the **Grand admin consent confirmation** pop-up, click **Yes.** See image.

Click **Azure Onboarding** to download the template as a ZIP file and extract it to your local system.

The ZIP file contains multiple Terraform files that contain policies and permissions required for the DSPM to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant.

Run the template in the Microsoft Entra tenant using the CLI app:

1. Update the downloaded `backend.tf` file with the storage container names where you want to store the Terraform state files. See image.
  - **resource_group_name**: Enter the resource group name.
  - **storage_account_name**: Enter the storage account name.
  - **container_name**: Enter the container name.
2. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
3. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To connect to your Microsoft Entra tenant: `az login --tenant <tenant ID>`See image. You are directed to a web browser to authorize the Microsoft Entra tenant. Select your account to confirm the authorization. See image. The command output returns the subscriptions available within your Microsoft Entra tenant.
  2. To set the subscription where you want to run the Terraform template: `az account set --subscription <subscription ID>`
  3. (Optional) To verify if the subscription is accurately set: `az account show`
  4. To initialize the working directory and apply Terraform configuration: `terraform init`See image.
  5. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`For **Enter a value**: Enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3"]`
  6. To run the script: `terraform apply`For **Enter a value**: Enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3"]`Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`. See image.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-compliance-frameworks","lastmod":"2026-04-09T22:11Z","nid":"1529784"} -->
## Managing Compliance Frameworks

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-compliance-frameworks
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Compliance > Managing Compliance Frameworks
- Last modified: 2026-04-09T22:11Z
- Summary: How to edit, delete, enable, or disable frameworks in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can enable or disable a predefined framework and edit, delete, enable, or disable a custom framework.

## Enabling or Disabling a Compliance Framework

Failed policies are not calculated for disabled frameworks.

When you click a disabled framework, you are directed to the Configuration tab and the Summary, Policies, and Resources tabs are disabled.

To enable or disable a compliance framework:

1. Go to **Analytics**>**Data Security**>**DSPM** >**Compliance**.
2. On the **Compliance**page, click the **Actions**()icon for the required compliance framework.
3. Select **Enable**or **Disable**. See image. The disabled frameworks are displayed at the end and grayed out.

## Editing a Custom Compliance Framework

To edit a custom compliance framework:

1. Go to **Analytics**>**Data Security**>**DSPM** >**Compliance**.
2. On the **Compliance**page, click the **Actions**()icon for the required compliance framework and select **Edit**. See image. You are directed to the **Summary**page.
3. On the **Summary**page, change the **Framework Name** or **Framework Description** as required.
4. Click the **Edit**icon for **Categories**, **Policies**,or **DLP Engines,**and update the fields as required. See image.
5. Click **Finish**.

## Deleting a Custom Compliance Framework

To delete a custom compliance framework:

1. Go to **Analytics**>**Data Security**>**DSPM** >**Compliance**.
2. On the **Compliance**page, click the **Actions**() icon for the required compliance framework and select **Delete**. See image.
3. On the **Delete Framework** window, enter `CONFIRM`, and then click **Delete**. The custom framework is deleted from the Zscaler Admin Console.

[Image: The Compliance dashboard with the list of frameworks and annotation around Actions icon and Edit option.]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-custom-tags","lastmod":"2026-07-02T07:06Z","nid":"1504756"} -->
## Managing Custom Tags

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-custom-tags
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Cloud Account Management > Managing Custom Tags
- Last modified: 2026-07-02T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about how to manage custom tags in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Custom tags are key-value pairs that allow you to organize, identify, and distinguish the resources created and deployed by DSPM in your cloud environment. Custom tags are created and applied to the DSPM resources while deploying the templates.

You can add, edit, or delete the custom tags, as required.

You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Custom tags must match the syntax used by cloud service providers to prevent errors while reading the tags. Follow these guidelines while adding custom tags:

- AWS
- Azure
- GCP

- Keys and values are case-sensitive.
- Custom tags can start with any supported character, including lowercase letters, uppercase letters, numbers, spaces, or special characters (`+ = @ _ / : . -`).
- Custom tags shouldn't start with `aws`.
- Keys must have a minimum of 1 character and not exceed 127 characters, and values must not exceed 256 characters.
- The values field can be empty.

- Keys are case-insensitive.
- Keys can include lowercase letters, uppercase letters, numbers, spaces, or special characters (`! @ # ^ * () _ {} : ; ' | . , [] ` ~ + = @ _ -`).
- Keys must have a minimum of 1 character and not exceed 128 characters.
- Values cannot exceed 256 characters.
- Values can include lowercase letters, uppercase letters, numbers, spaces, or special characters (`% & ? / > <`)

- Keys and values must include only lowercase letters, numbers, or special characters (`_ or -)`.
- Keys must start with a lowercase letter.
- Keys must have a minimum of 1 character and not exceed 63 characters.
- The values field can be empty.

Do not use the following predefined tags that are automatically assigned to the DSPM resources:

- z-dspm-tenant-id
- z-dspm-tenant-name
- z-dspm-resource
- z-lp-resource-type
- z-dspm-integration-id
- z-dspm-scanner-resource
- z-dspm-scan-id
- azure
- aws
- microsoft
- windows

## Adding Custom Tags

To add custom tags:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Manage Custom Tags** from the drop-down menu. See image.
4. On the **Manage Custom Tags** page, enter the key and value for the tag. See image.
5. Click **Add More**, and enter key-value pairs to add more tags.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **Apply Changes** page, download and deploy the template.
8. Click **Done**. See image. You can see the number of custom tags added on the [Overview](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarding-status)page.

## Editing Custom Tags

When you modify a custom tag and deploy the templates, the new custom tag overrides the existing custom tag, and the resources are updated with the modified tags.

To edit custom tags:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Manage Custom Tags** from the drop-down menu. See image.
4. On the **Manage Custom Tags** page, modify the key and value for the required tag. See image.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Apply Changes** page, download and deploy the templates.
7. Click **Done**.

## Deleting Custom Tags

When you delete custom tags, the tags are removed from the resources after you deploy the templates.

To delete custom tags:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Manage Custom Tags** from the drop-down menu.
4. On the **Manage Custom Tags** page, click the **Delete** icon for the custom tag that you want to delete. See image.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Apply Changes** page, download and deploy the templates.
7. Click **Done**.

## Managing Data Events

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-data-events
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Managing Data Events
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:52Z
- Summary: How to manage data events in the Zscaler Admin Console.

Data events provide information on the activities performed on or within AWS data stores, such as reading or writing to an S3 bucket, GetObject API operations, etc. DSPM supports ingestion of data events to analyze the activity logs.

## Managing Data Events Configuration for an Organization

To manage data events configuration for an organization:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the onboarded account. See image.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Manage Data Events**. See image.
4. On the **Configure Data Events** page, click the toggle to enable or disable data events: When disabled, DSPM stops collecting data events from the S3 bucket.
  - Enable
  - Disable

## Managing Data Events Configuration for Single or Multiple Accounts

To manage data events configuration for single or multiple accounts:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the AWS account and then select the **Accounts** tab. See image.
3. Choose one of the following options:
  - To manage data events for a single account: Click the **Actions** icon for the account you want to update data events on, then select **Manage Data Events**. See image.
  - To manage data events for multiple accounts:
    1. Select the checkboxes for the required accounts.
    2. From the **Actions**drop-down menu, select **Manage Data Events.** See image.
4. In the **Configure Data Events** window, click the toggle to enable or disable data events.
  - Enable
  - Disable

1. Under **Storage Information**, select one of the following:
  - **Use the same S3 bucket details provided for management events**: If the data events need to be stored in the same S3 bucket where the management events are stored. See image.
  - **Use a new S3 bucket**: If the data events need to be stored in a different S3 bucket: See image.
    - **CloudTrail Type**: Select the **OrgCloudTrail**checkbox, if it is an organization CloudTrail.
    - **CloudTrail Bucket Name**: Enter the S3 bucket name where the CloudTrail events are logged.
    - **Prefix**(Optional): Enter the prefix specified in the CloudTrail bucket path, if any.
    - **Bucket Account ID**: Enter the AWS account ID where the CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.
2. On the **Apply Changes** page: See image.
  1. Select the template type (**CloudFormation**or **Terraform**).
  2. Download the **Data Events** template and run it on the account where the specified CloudTrail S3 bucket is present.

1. Click **Next**.
2. On the **Apply Changes** page, click **Done**.

See image.

DSPM identifies files and tables containing [sensitive data](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-sensitive-data-details) and generates evidence data for review. You can configure an AWS S3 bucket or Azure storage account container, to store these classified evidence data snippets. You can also use an existing storage account or S3 bucket present in one of the [regions selected](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization#step3) while onboarding or allow DSPM to create a new one in the orchestrator account.

The S3 bucket or storage account container cannot be changed after it is added. You can only enable or disable the evidence configuration.

To manage evidence configuration:

This is required when multiple users need to apply Terraform from different IP addresses. To add your IP address: Sign in to the Azure portal and go to **Key vaults**.; On the **Key vaults** page, search and select the key vault created in the orchestrator account. See image.; In the left-side navigation, go to **Settings**> **Networking**.; On the **Firewalls and virtual networks** tab: Select **Allow public access from specific virtual networks and IP addresses**.; In the **Firewall**section, click **Add your client IP address** and enter your system's IP address.See image.; Click **Apply**.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-evidence-rules","lastmod":"2026-07-02T07:06Z","nid":"1540803"} -->
## Managing Evidence Rules

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-evidence-rules
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > On-Premises Data Centers and Scanners > Evidence > Managing Evidence Rules
- Last modified: 2026-07-02T07:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to edit, delete, enable, disable, or validate evidence rules.

You can enable, disable, edit, delete, or validate an evidence rule as required.

- Enabling or Disabling an Evidence Rule
- Editing an Evidence Rule
- Deleting an Evidence Rule
- Validating an Evidence Rule

You can enable or disable an evidence rule as required.

Evidence data is cached for 60 minutes. If you disable a rule, evidence data continues to be collected and stored for 60 minutes. When disabled, evidence collection is not started until the 60-minute cache is cleared.

To enable or disable an evidence rule:

1. Go to **Policies**> **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Evidence Settings**.
2. Select the toggle under the **Enable/Disable** column to enable or disable the evidence rule. See image.
3. Read the confirmation message that appears, then click **Enable Evidence Setting** or **Disable Evidence Setting** to apply the changes.

1. Go to **Policies**> **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Evidence Settings**.
2. Click the **Actions**icon and select **Edit**. See image.
3. On the **Edit Evidence Rule** page, modify the configuration as required.
4. Download and deploy the template on your account to grant access to the evidence bucket.
5. Click **Done**.

1. Go to **Policies**> **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Evidence Settings**.
2. Click the **Actions**icon and select **Delete**. See image.
3. In the **Delete Evidence Rule** window, enter `CONFIRM` and click **Delete**.

DSPM validates the evidence rules every 4 hours to verify if the template is deployed and the connection to the S3 bucket via IAM role is successful. You can also manually validate to verify the connection. Evidence data is collected in the S3 bucket only if the DSPM connection is successful.

The Connection Status can be one of the following:

- **Success**: The evidence template is deployed and DSPM connection to the S3 bucket is successful.
- **Pending**: The evidence template is yet to be deployed or validation is incomplete.
- **Failed**: DSPM failed to establish a connection to the S3 bucket (e.g., Template deployment failed, IAM role not created). You can view the details in the **Error**column.

To validate an evidence rule:

1. Go to **Policies**> **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Evidence Settings**.
2. Click the **Actions**icon and select **Validate**. See image. A pop-up message appears confirming that the validation is initiated. Based on the validation, the Connection Status is updated.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-ignore-alert-filters","lastmod":"2026-04-15T00:37Z","nid":"1477826"} -->
## Managing Ignore Alert Filters

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-ignore-alert-filters
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Alerts > Ignore Alert Filters > Managing Ignore Alert Filters
- Last modified: 2026-04-15T00:37Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage the DSPM ignore alert filters in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can edit, delete, enable, or disable the [ignore alert filters](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-ignore-filters) that you've added.

Editing or deleting the ignore alert filters impact only the newly triggered alerts.

## Editing an Ignore Alert Filter

To edit an ignore alert filter:

1. Go to **Administration**>**Alerts** > **Ignore Alert Filter**.
2. In the table, locate the ignore alert filter you want to edit, click the **Actions** icon (), and select **Edit**. See image.
3. On the **General Information** page, change the **Ignore Filter Name** or **Filter Description**as required, then click **Next**.
4. On the **Filter Scope** page, update the filters as required, then click **Next**.
5. Review the changes and click **Finish**. See image. A message appears indicating that the ignore alert filter is updated successfully.

## Deleting an Ignore Alert Filter

To delete an ignore alert filter:

1. Go to **Administration**>**Alerts** > **Ignore Alert Filter**.
2. In the table, locate the ignore alert filter you want to edit, click the **Actions** icon (), and select **Delete**. See image.
3. A confirmation message appears. Read the message and click **Delete**. See image. The ignore alert filter is deleted from the Zscaler Admin Console and is no longer available in the ignore alerts table.

## Enabling or Disabling Ignore Alert Filter

You can enable or disable the [ignore alert filters](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-ignore-filters) you've added.

By default, the ignore alert filter is enabled. If the selected filters of the filter scope are deleted (e.g., policies are deleted, accounts are offboarded, or the business unit is deleted), the ignore alert filter is disabled. You can enable the filter only after the filter scope is updated.

To enable or disable the ignore alert filter:

1. Go to **Administration**>**Alerts** > **Ignore Alert Filter**.
2. Click the toggle under the **State** column to enable or disable the ignore alert filter. See image.
3. A confirmation message appears indicating that the ignore alert filter is going to be enabled or disabled. Click **Enable** or **Disable** depending on the action. See image.

[Image: The Ignore Alert Filter page with annotation around the State column.]

[Image: The Disable Ignore Filter window]

[Image: The Actions icon with the list of actions available and annotation around the Edit option.]

[Image: The Actions icon with the list of actions available and annotation around the Delete option.]

[Image: The Summary page with the list of fields configured.]

[Image: The Delete ignore alert filter window.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-monitoring-scope-aws","lastmod":"2026-04-24T22:56Z","nid":"1478016"} -->
## Managing Monitoring Scope for AWS

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-monitoring-scope-aws
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Managing Monitoring Scope for AWS
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:56Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage the monitoring scope for AWS in the Zscaler Admin Console.

The monitoring scope refers to the AWS target accounts that are [onboarded](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization). When new accounts are added to your organization, you can onboard them to DSPM for monitoring data stores. You can add new accounts to the monitoring scope, but you cannot remove the existing target accounts.

Additionally, you can enable autodetection at the organization or organizational unit (OU) level. The autodetection feature enables DSPM to automatically detect and onboard any new accounts added to the organization or OU in the future. This eliminates the need to manually onboard new accounts to DSPM.

## Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or any role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

## Managing Monitoring Scope

To add new accounts to the monitoring scope:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the organization for which you want to add new target accounts. See image.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Monitoring & Autodetection** from the drop-down menu. See image.
  1. On the **Add to Monitoring Scope** page, select the accounts that you want to be monitored. See image. Enable **Autodetection** at the organization or OU level so DSPM can automatically detect and onboard any new accounts that are added in the future. Click **Next**. You must activate automatic deployment in AWS to automatically deploy stack instances for newly added account in the future.
  2. On the **Assign Business Units** page, change the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) for the OU if required, then click **Next**. See image.
  3. On the **Apply Changes** page, download the monitoring scope template and run it in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/). See image.
    - Template Type
    - Monitoring Scope
    - Autodetection
4. Click **Done**. The new target accounts are added to the monitoring scope. You can view all the organization's onboarded accounts in the [Accounts tab](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarded-account-details).

Select the **CloudFormation**or **Terraform**template.

- Run the CloudFormation template
- Run the Terraform template

- i. Download the monitoring scope template.
- ii. Update the StackSet.

Click **Monitoring Scope** to download the template as a ZIP file and extract it to your local system. The ZIP file contains two files:

- A CSV file that contains a list of target accounts that needs to be scanned.
- A YAML file that contains the policies and permissions required for DSPM to connect to the AWS organization.

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) root account and go to **CloudFormation**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **StackSets**. See image.
3. Identify the StackSet created for monitoring scope while [onboarding the organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization) and click **StackSet name**. See image.
4. Under **Actions**, click **Edit StackSet details**. See image.
5. On the **Choose a template** page: See image.
  - **Prerequisite - Prepare template**: Select **Replace current template**.
  - **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file**.
  - **Upload a template file**: Click **Choose file**, browse your folder and select the YAML file downloaded from the Zscaler Admin Console, then click **Open**.
6. Click **Next**.
7. On the **Specify StackSet Details** page, click **Next**.
8. On the **Configure StackSet options** page, click **Next**.
9. On the **Set deployment options** page: See image.
  - Select **Deploy to accounts**and then select **Deploy stacks in accounts**.
  - **Account numbers**: Add the new account numbers or upload the CSV file downloaded from the Zscaler Admin Console.
  - **Specify regions:**Select the regions that contain the data stores that you want to scan.
  - **Region concurrency**: Select **Sequential** to deploy the StackSets in a sequential order as specified in the **Specify regions**.
10. Click **Next**.
11. On the **Review** page, review the StackSet details and then select the **I acknowledge** checkbox to acknowledge AWS CloudFormation's creation of IAM resources with custom names. See image.
12. Click **Submit**. On the **Operations** tab, you can see the status of the StackSet execution. See image. On the **Stack Instances** tab, you can view the stack instances created for each account and region. To complete the StackSet execution, all the individual stack instances must be deployed successfully. See image.

- i. Download the monitoring scope template.
- ii. Copy the access keys of the target account.
- iii. Update and run the Terraform files.

Click **Monitoring Scope** to download the Terraform template as a ZIP file and extract it to your local system. The ZIP file contains the following files:

- A CSV file containing the list of target accounts that you want to be monitored.
- Multiple Terraform files that contains policies and permissions required for the DSPM to connect to the AWS organization.
- A README file that contains the instructions to run the template.

The access keys provide DSPM with administrator access to the target account from the AWS CLI.

1. Sign in to the AWS access portal and select the target account.
2. Click **Access keys**. See image.
3. Select the required tab (macOS/Linux, Windows, PowerShell) based on your operating system.
4. Under **Option 1: Set AWS environment variables**, click **Copy**and save the access keys. See image.

1. Update the downloaded Terraform files:
  - In the `parameters.auto.tfvars` file, under **regions**, enter the primary region of the target account. See image.
  - In the `backend.tf` file, add the name of the storage services where you want to store the Terraform state files. For example: See image.
    - **bucket**: Enter the name of the S3 bucket of the target account.
    - **region**: Enter the primary region of the target account.
    - **dynamoDB_table**: Enter the name of the dynamoDB table in the primary region of the target account.
2. Open the Command prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
3. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform files.
4. Paste the access keys you copied earlier and press `Enter`.
5. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the Terraform working directory: `terraform init`See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`
  3. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`See image. Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes`and press `Enter`. See image.

Review the list of OUs that you selected for autodetection.

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-monitoring-scope-gcp","lastmod":"2026-04-24T22:34Z","nid":"1498106"} -->
## Managing Monitoring Scope for GCP

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-monitoring-scope-gcp
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > GCP Cloud Accounts > Managing Monitoring Scope for GCP
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:34Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage the monitoring scope for GCP in the Zscaler Admin Console.

The monitoring scope refers to the GCP projects that are [onboarded](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-gcp-organization). When new projects are created in your GCP organization, you can onboard and add new projects to the monitoring scope.

You can also enable autodetection, which allows DSPM to automatically detect and onboard any new projects added in the future. This eliminates the need to manually onboard new projects to DSPM.

## Prerequisites

Be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or any role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

## Managing Monitoring Scope

To add new projects to the monitoring scope:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account to which you want to add new target projects.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Monitoring & Autodetection** from the drop-down menu. See image.
  1. On the **Add to Monitoring Scope** page, select the projects that you want to be monitored. Enable **Autodetection** so DSPM can automatically detect and onboard any new subscriptions that are added in the future. See image. Click **Next**. After a project has been added to the monitoring scope, you cannot remove it from the monitoring scope. If you want to stop monitoring a project, you need to delete the project from the DSPM organization. To learn more, see[Deleting an Onboarded Account](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/deleting-onboarded-account).
  2. On the **Assign Business Units** page, change the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) for the management group if required, then click **Next**. See image.
  3. On the **Apply Changes** page:
    - Monitoring Scope
    - Autodetection
  4. Click **Done**.

The new projects are added to the monitoring scope. You can view all the organization's onboarded projects on the [Projects tab](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarded-account-details).

The onboarding template includes policies and permissions to create custom roles in the GCP organization. This template provides DSPM with the permissions to access the organization.

- i. In the Zscaler Admin Console
- ii. On the Local System

Click **GCP Onboarding** to download the template as a ZIP file.

See image.

[Image: Download GCP Onboarding Template]

Update and run the template in the gcloud using the CLI app:

1. Extract the downloaded ZIP file to a local directory on your system.
2. Locate the `backend.tf` file within the extracted folder and open it in a text editor. See image.
3. Update the file by adding the name of the storage bucket and a preferred prefix where you would like to store the Terraform state files, and then, save and close the `backend.tf` file. See image.
4. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app on your local system.
5. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
6. Run the following commands:
  1. To initialize the working directory and apply the Terraform configuration: `terraform init`See image.
  2. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want DSPM to monitor and scan data in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`DSPM creates resources required for data scanning only in these specified regions. See image.
  3. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`For **Enter a value**, enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3", and so on.]`See image. For **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`. See image.

[Image: Terraform apply]

See image.

## Managing Monitoring Scope for Microsoft Azure

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-monitoring-scope-microsoft-azure
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Microsoft Azure Cloud Accounts > Managing Monitoring Scope for Microsoft Azure
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:46Z
- Summary: Information on how to manage the monitoring scope for Azure in the Zscaler Admin Console.

The monitoring scope refers to the Azure target subscriptions that are [onboarded](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant). When new subscriptions are added to your Microsoft Entra tenant, you can onboard and add these new subscriptions to the monitoring scope.

You can also enable autodetection, which allows DSPM to automatically detect and onboard any new subscriptions that are added in the future. This eliminates the need to manually onboard new subscriptions to DSPM.

## Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

## Managing Monitoring Scope

To add new subscriptions to the monitoring scope:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the tenant for which you want to add new target subscriptions.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Monitoring & Autodetection** from the drop-down menu. See image. The new subscriptions are added to the monitoring scope. You can view the tenant's onboarded subscriptions on the [Subscriptions tab](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-onboarded-account-details).
  1. On the **Add Subscriptions to Monitoring Scope** page, select the subscriptions that you want to be monitored. Enable **Autodetection,** so DSPM can automatically detect and onboard any new subscriptions that are added in the future. Click **Next**. After a subscription has been added to the monitoring scope, you cannot remove it from the monitoring scope. If you want to stop monitoring a subscription, you need to delete the subscription from the DSPM tenant. To learn more, see [Deleting an Onboarded Tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/deleting-onboarded-account). See image.
  2. On the **Assign Business Units** page, change the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) for the management group if required, then click **Next**. See image.
  3. On the **Apply Changes** page:
    - Monitoring Scope
    - Autodetection
  4. Click **Done**.

The onboarding template contains the policies and permissions required to create custom roles in the Microsoft Entra tenant providing DSPM with read-only access to collect data for various services.

To download and run the template, do the following:

- i. In the Zscaler Admin Console
- ii. On the Local System

Click **Azure Onboarding** to download the template as a ZIP file. Extract the file to your local system and create a new folder to store the extracted files. The ZIP file contains multiple Terraform files that contain policies and permissions required for the DSPM to connect to the Microsoft Entra tenant.

See image.

Run the template in the Microsoft Entra tenant using the CLI app:

1. Update the `backend.tf` filewith the name of the storage containers that you used while [onboarding the tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant) to store the Terraform state files. See image.
  - **resource_group_name**: Enter the resource group name.
  - **storage_account_name**: Enter the storage account name.
  - **container_name**: Enter the container name.
2. Open the Command Prompt or any other CLI app in your local system.
3. Switch to the directory containing the downloaded Terraform file.
4. Run the following commands:
  1. To connect to your Microsoft Entra tenant: `az login --tenant <tenant ID>`See image. You are directed to a web browser to authorize the Microsoft Entra tenant. Select your account to confirm the authorization. The command output returns the subscriptions available within your Microsoft Entra tenant.
  2. To set the subscription where you want to run the Terraform template: `az account set --subscription <subscription ID>`
  3. (Optional) To verify if the subscription is accurately set: `az account show`
  4. To initialize the working directory and apply Terraform configuration: `terraform init`See image.
  5. To verify the changes in the Terraform configuration: `terraform plan`For **Enter a value**: Enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3"]`
  6. To run the Terraform script: `terraform apply`For **Enter a value**: Enter the regions where you want to deploy the template in the following format: `["region name1", "region name2", "region name3"]`Under **Do you want to perform these actions?**, enter `yes` and then press `Enter`. See image. For **Enter IP**, enter the IP address of the system on which you are running the template.

Review the list of management groups that you selected for autodetection.

See image.

## Managing Orchestrator Network

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-orchestrator-network
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Custom Network Configuration > Managing Orchestrator Network
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:32Z
- Summary: Information on how to update the orchestrator and network details in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can modify the orchestrator network details when an existing orchestrator network is being decommissioned, deleted, or if an incorrect network was selected during onboarding. After changing the orchestrator network, you must rerun the orchestrator template to update the deployment. DSPM validates the template deployment and updates the [orchestrator status](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/viewing-orchestrator-status) accordingly.

This option is available only when the DSPM Connection Status is failed for the custom network configuration type.

## Prerequisites

You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the DSPM Admin Portal.

## Modifying the Orchestrator Network

To modify the orchestrator network configuration:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account.
3. From the **Manage** drop-down menu, select **Managing Orchestrator Networks**. See image.
4. On the **Manage Orchestrator Networks** page, update the orchestrator network:
  - AWS
  - Azure
5. Click **Done**.

After the templates are deployed, the regions are updated in the DSPM Admin Portal and subsequent data scans are performed on the resources in the selected regions.

1. **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator template.
2. **Subnet ARN**: Enter the subnet where the scanner instances must be launched.
3. **Security Group ID**: Enter the identifier (ID) of the security group that controls network traffic to and from the instances. See image.
4. Click **Next**.
5. On the **Apply Changes** page, [download and run the orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization#orchestrator-template-step4). See image.

1. **Select Orchestrator Region**: Select a region where you want to deploy the orchestrator template.
2. **Subnet ID**: Enter the subnet where the scanner instances must be launched.
3. **Network Security Group ID**: Enter the identifier (ID) of the security group that controls network traffic to and from the instances.
4. **Storage Account Name**: Enter a unique name for the storage account. This storage account is used to store the activity logs of the target subscriptions and is created while deploying the [onboarding template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#azureonboardingtemplate). DSPM validates the uniqueness of the storage account name. If the name is already registered with [Microsoft.Storage](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#reg-microsoft-storage), DSPM displays an error message. See image. The storage account name must not exceed 16 characters. See image.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Apply Changes** page, [download and run the orchestrator template](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#grantpermission). If you are using a new subnet from a different VNet, run the following command before deploying the new template: `terraform destroy -target module.scale_set.azurerm_linux_virtual_machine_scale_set.orchestrator_scale_set` See image.

[Image: Configuring Region Networks Page]

## Managing Policies

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-policies
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Data Posture Policies > Managing Policies
- Last modified: 2026-04-21T21:06Z
- Summary: Information on how to enable, disable, edit, delete, or clone policies in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can enable, disable, edit, delete, change policy severity, or clone a policy as required.

- Enabling or Disabling a Single Policy
- Enabling or Disabling Bulk Policies
- Editing a Policy
- Deleting a Policy
- Cloning a Policy
- Changing Policy Severity

You can enable or disable an individual policy or multiple policies as required.

New alerts are not generated for disabled policies. However, the status of the existing alerts remains unchanged.

To enable or disable a single policy:

1. Go to **Policies**>**Data Protection**>**Policy**> **Data Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, do any of the following:
  - Click the **Actions** icon for the required policy, then select **Enable** or **Disable**. See image.
  - Select the checkbox for the required policy. Select **Enable** or **Disable** from the **Actions** drop-down menu that appears on the page. See image.
3. In the **Enable Policy** or **Disable Policy** window, select the checkbox to confirm that you want to proceed. See image.
4. Click **Enable** or **Disable**.

To enable or disable bulk security policies:

1. Go to **Policies**>**Data Protection**>**Policy**> **Data Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, select the checkboxes for the required policies. The **Actions** drop-down appears on the page. See image.
3. From the **Actions** drop-down menu, select **Enable** or **Disable**.
4. In the **Enable Policy** or **Disable Policy** window, select the checkbox to confirm that you want to proceed. See image.
5. Click **Enable** or **Disable**.

[Image: Enable a policy for a resource]

[Image: Enable or disable multiple policies]

[Image: Enable or disable multiple policies]

[Image: Disable a policy]

Editing a custom data posture policy might have an impact on the alerts that DSPM generates. If you edit any custom policy, such as the policy title or remediation procedure, the new information is displayed on the [Alerts page](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-alerts) and the dashboard. If you edit the custom policy query logic, DSPM determines that the custom policy has changed and closes all existing alerts, and generates new alerts based on the updated custom policy query logic.

You can edit or delete only the custom policies. Predefined policies cannot be edited or deleted.

To edit a custom data posture policy:

1. Go to **Policies**>**Data Protection**>**Policy**> **Data Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, click the **Actions** icon for the required custom policy.
3. Click **Edit**. You are directed to the **Query Builder** page.
4. On the **Query Builder** page, [edit the query](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/creating-custom-policies)as required.
5. When you are done editing the query, click **Test Run**. The query results are displayed in the **Policy Test Result** window. See image.
6. Click **Accept and Proceed**.
7. On the **Remediation Procedure** page, click **Add Remediation Procedure**.
8. Enter the remediation steps in Markdown format, then click **Save**. If you've already added the remediation procedure, then click the **Edit** icon to modify the text, if required. See image.
9. Click **Next**.
10. On the **Severity and Description** page, edit any of the values as required. See image.
11. Click **Save Changes**.

When you delete a custom policy, all alerts previously generated by the policy are closed.

To delete a custom data posture policy:

1. Go to **Policies**>**Data Protection**>**Policy**> **Data Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, click the **Actions** icon for the required custom policy. See image.
3. Read the confirmation message, then click **Delete**. See image.

[Image: The query result]

[Image: Add the remediation steps]

[Image: Select the Delete option]

[Image: Confirm to delete a policy]

You can clone a predefined or an existing custom policy by reusing its query structure and modifying some parameters, as required, to create another custom policy.

To clone a policy:

1. Go to **Policies**>**Data Protection**>**Policy**> **Data Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, click the **Actions** icon () and select the **Clone** option for the required policy. See image. You cannot clone policies that are temporarily hidden.
3. In the **Duplicate Policy** window, select the checkbox to confirm that you want to proceed, then click **Clone**. See image. You are directed to the **Query Builder** page.
4. On the **Query Builder** page, add additional predicates to the query if required. See image.
5. Continue with the remaining steps to [create the policy](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/creating-custom-policies). The new policy is created and displayed on the **Policy** page.

[Image: Clone a policy]

[Image: Confirmation message]

[Image: Add additional parameters to the query]

You can change the severity of a data posture policy as required. When you change the policy severity, it impacts the alert risk level that is triggered for any findings by this policy.

You cannot edit, delete, or change the severity level for predefined policies.

To change the policy severity:

1. Go to **Policies**>**Data Protection**>**Policy**> **Data Posture Policies**.
2. On the **Policy** page, select the checkbox of the required policy. See image.
3. Click the **Actions** drop-down menu and select **Change Severity**. See image.
4. In the **Change Policy Severity** window, select one of the following options from the **Policy Severity** drop-down menu: See image.
  - Critical
  - High
  - Medium
  - Low
5. Click the **I understand the consequences and want to proceed** checkbox.
6. Click **Change**. You have now successfully changed the policy severity.

[Image: Shows the data posture policies on the Policy page.]

[Image: Shows the actions that you can perform on the selected policy.]

[Image: Change the severity of the selected policy.]
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-premises-data-center","lastmod":"2026-05-24T07:06Z","nid":"1526566"} -->
## Managing an On-Premises Data Center

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-premises-data-center
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > On-Premises Data Centers and Scanners > On-Premises Data Centers > Managing an On-Premises Data Center
- Last modified: 2026-05-24T07:06Z
- Summary: Information about how to manage an on-premises data center in the Zscaler Admin Console

You can add, modify, or delete [on-premises data centers](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-center) on DSPM as required.

## Prerequisites

Make sure the following prerequisites are met:

- [Onboard the account using a custom model](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#SelectNetworkConfiguration) to establish network connectivity to the on-premises data center.
- Modify security groups to allow connections from the scanner or orchestrator subnets.
- Create a [custom role with required permissions to configure SQL authentication.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-sql-authentication-unmanaged-databases)
- Provide SQL connection strings and authentication credentials for our solution to access the on-premises data centers.

## Adding On-Premises Data Center

To add an on-premises data center to scan for sensitive data and posture risks:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **On-Premises Data Centers**.
2. On the **On-Premises Data Centers** page, click **Add Data Center**. See image.
3. In the **Add New On-Premises Data Center** drawer: See image.
  - Data Center
  - Connect Scanners to the Data Center
4. Click **Save**. The **Add Data Center** window appears.
5. In the **Add Data Center** window, click **Confirm and Save**. See image.

The on-premises data center is added and displayed on the [On-Premises Data Centers](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-center) page.

To configure scan settings to scan the sensitive data in the on-premises data center, see [Configuring Scan Settings for On-Premises Data Center](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/configuring-scan-settings-premise-unmanaged-database).

1. **Data Center Name**: Enter a unique name for the on-premises data center.
2. **Location**: Search for and select the region where the data center is located.
3. **Business Unit**: Assign the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) to the data center.

**Select On-Premises Scanner Integration**: Select an existing [on-premises scanner integration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-premises-scanner-integrations) to connect with the data center.

[Image: Add Data Center confirmation window for data centers with an annotation around Confirm and Save button.]

[Image: Add New On-Premises Data Center with required fields to add a data center.]

[Image: On-Premises Data Centers page with an annotation around the Add Data Center button.]

## Editing an On-Premises Data Center

To edit an on-premises data center:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **On-Premises Data Centers**.
2. Do one of the following: The **Edit Data Center** window appears.
  - Click **Actions** (), and select **Edit** for the required data center. See image.
  - Click the name of the data center to go to the [On-Premises Data Center details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-center) page, then click **Actions** and select **Edit**. See image.
3. In the **Edit Data Center** window, click **Proceed** to continue. See image.
4. On the **Edit On-Premises Data Center** drawer, update the following: See image.
  - **Business Unit**: Update the [business unit](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-business-units) for the data center.
  - **Connect Scanners to the Data Center**: Update the scanner integrations that must be linked to the data center.
    - **Select On-Premises Scanner Integration**: Update an existing [on-premises scanner integration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-premises-scanner-integrations) to connect with the data center.
5. Click **Save**.

The on-premises data center is updated.

Changes made to the on-premises data center configuration only take effect at the next scheduled scan.

[Image: The on-premises data center page with information relating to the data center and cloud network association..]

[Image: Confirm editing on-premises data center window]

[Image: On-Premises Data Centers page with the Actions menu open, and showing the Edit option annotated.]

[Image: On-Premises Data Center details page with a highlighted edit icon.]

## Deleting an On-Premises Data Center

To delete an on-premises data center:

Deleting an on-premises data center is restricted if it is associated with any [unmanaged databases](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-unmanaged-database). The **Delete** option is grayed out in such cases.

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **On-Premises Data Centers**.
2. Do one of the following: The **Delete Data Center** window appears.
  - Click **Actions** (), and select **Delete**for the required data center. See image.
  - Click the name of the data center to go to the [On-Premises Data Center details](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-center) page, then click **Actions** and select **Delete**. See image.
3. In the **Delete Data Center** window, read the message, and then enter `CONFIRM` in the text box. See image.
4. Click **Delete Server**.

The on-premises data center is deleted from the Zscaler Admin Console.

[Image: Unmanaged Databases page with the Actions menu open, and showing the Delete option annotated.]

[Image: Unmanaged Databases details page with a highlighted delete icon.]

[Image: Confirming deletion of an unmanaged database server]

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/managing-regions","lastmod":"2026-04-24T22:25Z","nid":"1507481"} -->
## Managing Regions

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-regions
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > Cloud Account Management > Managing Regions
- Last modified: 2026-04-24T22:25Z
- Summary: Information about how to manage regions in the Zscaler Admin Console.

You can choose to deploy scanner instances in specific regions to control resource allocation and costs. This allows you to limit the deployment of scanner instances in selected regions and scan for sensitive data.

You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or a custom role with the Configure Monitoring Scope permission in the Zscaler Admin Console.

To select the regions:

1. Go to **Policies** > **Common Configuration** > **DSPM** > **Cloud Accounts**.
2. Select the cloud account.
3. Click **Manage**, and then select **Manage Regions**. See image.
4. On the **Manage Regions** page:
  - If you select the Zscaler network configuration while onboarding the cloud account
  - If you select the custom network configuration while onboarding the cloud account
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Apply Changes** page:
  - For AWS
  - For Azure
  - For GCP
7. Click **Done**.

After the templates are deployed, the regions are updated in the Zscaler Admin Console and subsequent [data scans](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings) are performed on the resources in the selected regions.

Download the deploy the GCP Onboarding template. To learn more, see [Onboarding a GCP Organization](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-gcp-organization#download_gcp_onboarding).

Download the orchestrator template and extract it to your local system.

To deploy the CloudFormation template:

1. Sign in to the orchestrator account in the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **CloudFormation**> **StackSets**.
2. Identify and select the StackSet created while running the orchestrator template.
3. Click **Actions**and select **Add stacks to StackSet**. See image.
4. On the **Set deployment options** page: See image.
  - **Add stacks to stack set**: Select **Deploy new stacks**.
  - **Accounts**:
    - **Deployment locations**: Select **Deploy stacks in accounts**.
    - **Account numbers**: Enter the AWS account ID of the orchestrator account.
    - **Specify regions**: Select the new regions that you selected in the Zscaler Admin Console to deploy the resources required for scanning.
5. Click **Next**.
6. On the **Specify overrides** page, click **Next**.
7. On the **Review** page, review the StackSet details and click **Submit**. The new regions are added to the StackSet. On the **Operations**tab, you can view the status of the StackSet. On the **Stack instances** tab, you can view the stack instances created for each region you selected.
8. Click **Actions**and select **Edit StackSet details**. See image.
9. On the **Choose a template** page: See image.
  1. **Prerequisite - Prepare template**: Select **Replace current template.**
  2. **Specify template**: Select **Upload a template file** and click **Choose file**. Browse to the location where the template file is extracted, select the YAML file, and then click **Open**.
10. Click **Next**.
11. On the **Specify StackSet details** page, click **Next**.
12. On the **Configure StackSet options** page, select the **I acknowledge** checkbox and then click **Next**.
13. On the **Set deployment options** page: See image.
  - **Deployment locations**: Select **Deploy stacks in accounts**.
  - **Account numbers**: Enter the AWS account ID of the orchestrator account that you selected in the Zscaler Admin Console.
  - **Specify regions**: Select the new and the existing regions to deploy the resources required for scanning.
14. On the **Review** page, review the StackSet details and click **Submit**.

Download and deploy the Azure Onboarding template. To learn more, see [Onboarding a Microsoft Azure Tenant](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#grantpermidspm).

Select the checkbox for the regions where you want to deploy the resources. For each region, update the following details.

- For AWS
- For Azure

- Enter the **Subnet ARN**.
- Enter the **Security Group ID**.
- Add the **DB Subnet Group ARN** (if required).

See image.

- Enter the **Subnet ID**.
- Enter the **Network Security Group ID**.
- Add the **Postgres Delegated Subnet ID** (if required).
- Enter the **Storage Account Resource ID** (This field is displayed only if you have enabled the option to create storage accounts in each region while onboarding the Azure accounts using a [custom configuration](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-microsoft-azure-tenant#custom_configuration).)

See image.

Select the checkbox for the regions where you want to deploy the resources. This allows DSPM to monitor the resources only in the selected regions.

See image.

## Managing Vulnerabilities in AWS Accounts

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/managing-vulnerabilities-aws-accounts
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Scan Rules > Vulnerability Scanning > Managing Vulnerabilities in AWS Accounts
- Last modified: 2026-07-01T23:37Z
- Summary: Information about vulnerability scanning of AWS accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console.

DSPM scans your Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud accounts to detect vulnerabilities and displays the scan results on the [Resource Inventory page](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-inventory).

Vulnerability scanning is supported for both AWS-managed and customer-managed encryption. However, to support AWS-managed encryption, at least one customer-managed key should be present in the region.

## Supported Regions

DSPM supports the vulnerability scanning of AWS accounts in the [supported AWS regions](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/supported-data-stores-file-types-and-regions#aws-region). To learn more, see [Supported Data Stores, File Types, and Regions](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/supported-data-stores-file-types-and-regions).
<!-- /ZS-ARTICLE -->

- Last modified: 2026-06-26T00:29Z
- Summary: Information about vulnerability scanning of Azure accounts in the Zscaler Admin Console.

DSPM scans your Microsoft Azure cloud accounts to detect vulnerabilities and displays the scan results on the [Resource Inventory page](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-data-inventory).

- DSPM supports the scanning of workloads that are created from images present in Azure Compute Gallery and Azure Marketplace.
- DSPM does not support the vulnerability scanning of Azure workloads created from unmanaged OS disks (.vhd).

<!-- ZS-ARTICLE {"url":"/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization","lastmod":"2026-07-07T09:31Z","nid":"1474896"} -->
## Onboarding an AWS Organization

- Source: https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/onboarding-aws-organization
- Product: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)
- Path: Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) Help > Cloud Accounts Onboarding > AWS Cloud Accounts > AWS Organization > Onboarding an AWS Organization
- Last modified: 2026-07-07T09:31Z
- Summary: Information on how to onboard an AWS organization in the Zscaler Admin Console.

[Watch a video about Onboarding an AWS Organization.](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/iframe/08mtpwfaqc)

You can onboard an AWS organization and its associated accounts. DSPM monitors and [scans](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings) the [data stores](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/supported-data-stores) (e.g., S3, EC2 instances, RDS instances and clusters) in the onboarded accounts to identify sensitive data and vulnerabilities.

## Onboarding Workflow

The onboarding process is illustrated in the following image:

[Image: The AWS organization onboarding workflow represented in a flow chart.]

## Prerequisites

Before onboarding an AWS organization, ensure you have completed the following:

- Identify an AWS account as the orchestrator account. The DSPM template is deployed in this account to scan the data in the target accounts.
- Identify the target AWS accounts that need to be monitored and protected. DSPM defines these target accounts as monitoring scope.
- You must be assigned either an [Administrator role](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/predefined-roles-and-permissions) or any role with Add Accounts permissions in the Zscaler Admin Console.
- Configure[CloudTrail](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-cloudtrail) for management and data events for DSPM to perform incremental [data scans](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/about-scan-settings) on S3 buckets. This is an optional step if you want to configure CloudTrail while onboarding. To enable data event for S3 buckets:
  1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **CloudTrail**.
  2. Under **Trails**, click the name of the CloudTrail that must be used to store data events.
  3. Under **Data events**, click **Edit**. See image.
  4. For **All current and future S3 buckets**, select the **Write** checkbox. See image.
  5. Click **Save changes**.
- Identify the template type you want to use:
  - CloudFormation Template
  - Terraform Template

## Onboarding an AWS Organization

To onboard an AWS organization:

1. [Provide AWS organization details.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/adding-organization-details)
2. [Deploy the tree discovery template.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/deploying-aws-tree-discovery-template)
3. [Select the orchestrator account, monitoring scope, and business unit.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/selecting-aws-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope)
4. [Deploy the orchestrator and monitoring scope templates.](https://help.zscaler.com/dspm/deploying-orchestrator-and-monitoring-scope-templates)

To use the CloudFormation template:

- Understand the following AWS concepts:
  - **Stacks**: A collection of AWS resources that can be managed as a single unit. They are required to run the DSPM templates. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacks.html).
  - **StackSets**: An entity that allows you to create, update, or delete stacks across multiple AWS accounts and regions using a CloudFormation template. StackSets are required to run the DSPM templates. It also allows you to add a new region to an existing StackSet (e.g., add secondary regions for orchestrator setup). To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stackinstances-create.html).
  - **Identity and Access Management (IAM) Roles**: IAM roles are entities that assign specific permissions to allow trusted identities to perform actions in AWS. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html).
  - **Subnet**: A subnet is a range of IP addresses in your VPC that can be connected to the internet, other VPCs, or data centers. To learn more, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/how-it-works.html).
- Create the following IAM roles in the orchestrator account to establish a trust relationship between the orchestrator account and target accounts. The IAM roles are required to create stacks and StackSets that are used to deploy the DSPM template in the AWS organization.
  - AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole
  - AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole
- Create the AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole IAM role on all the target accounts with a trust relationship with the root account and the AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole role. This is required to deploy the DSPM templates on the target accounts via the root account.
- Ensure that each AWS region has at least two default subnets in the default virtual private clouds (VPC). DSPM creates subnets to launch AWS cloud resources (e.g., EC2 instances, S3 buckets) in specific subnets.

To use the Terraform template:

- Install the following on your local system:
  - Terraform CLI to run the Terraform templates.
  - AWS CLI 2.22 version or later to connect to the AWS organization. For instructions on installing or updating AWS CLI, refer to the [AWS documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html).
- Identify the storage services in the primary region of the orchestrator account to store the Terraform state files. You can use an existing storage service or create a new one. For example:
  - AWS S3 Bucket
  - DynamoDB Table

To create an AWS S3 bucket:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **S3**.
2. Click **Create bucket**.
3. Under **Bucket name**, enter a unique name to the S3 bucket.
4. Click **Create bucket**.

To create a DynamoDB table:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **DynamoDB**.
2. Click **Create table**.
3. On the **Table details** page:
  - **Table name**: Enter a unique name to the table.
  - **Partition key**: Enter **LockID**.
4. Click **Create table**.

This IAM role with admin permissions creates a trust relationship with the CloudFormation service.

To create the AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole role:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **IAM**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Roles**.
3. Click **Create Role**.
4. In the **Select trusted entity** page:
  - **Trusted entity type**: Select the **AWS account** tile.
  - **An AWS account**: Select **This account (<root account ID>).**
5. Click **Next**.
6. In the **Add permissions**page, select the **AdministratorAccess** policy from the table and click **Next**.
7. In the **Name, review, and create**page, under **Role name**, enter the role name as **AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole**.
8. Click **Create role**.
9. On the **Permissions** tab, click **Add permissions** and then select **Create inline policy** from the drop-down menu.
  1. On the **Specify permissions** page, under **Policy editor**, select **JSON**.
  2. Copy the following JSON text and paste it in the **Policy editor** text box. `{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Action": [ "sts:AssumeRole" ], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:iam::*:role/AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole" ], "Effect": "Allow" } ] }`
10. Click **Next**.
11. On the **Review and create** page, under **Policy name**, enter `AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationPolicy`.
12. Click **Create policy**.

This IAM role creates a trust relationship with the administrator account and the AWSCloudFormationStackSetAdministrationRole IAM role.

To create the AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole role:

1. Sign in to the [AWS Management Console](https://aws.amazon.com/console/) and go to **IAM**.
2. In the left-side navigation, select **Roles**.
3. Click **Create Role**.
4. In the **Select trusted entity** page:
  - **Trusted entity type**: Select the **AWS account** tile.
  - **An AWS account**: Select **This account (<root account ID>)**.
5. Click **Next**.
6. In the **Add permissions**page, select **AdministratorAccess**and **SystemAdministrator** policy from the table and click **Next**.
7. In the **Name, review, and create**page, under **Role name**, enter the role name as **AWSCloudFormationStackSetExecutionRole**.
8. Click **Create role**.
9. On the **Permissions** tab, click **Add permissions** and then select **Create inline policy**to provide additional permissions from the drop-down menu.
  1. On the **Specify permissions** page, under **Policy editor**, select **JSON**.
  2. Copy the following JSON text and paste it in the **Policy editor** text box. `{ "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Effect": "Allow", "Action": [ "cloudformation:*" ], "Resource": "*" } ] }`
  3. Click **Next**.
  4. On the **Review and create** page, under **Policy name**, enter `ScannerCFT`.
  5. Click **Create policy**.

[Image: Enable S3 data events for CloudTrail]

[Image: Edit Data Events for S3 bucket]
